### F-053 Asking RenderQuality for debanding switches the Catmull-Rom kernel off on both GPU renderers, and the API does not say so.

**Severity:** medium · **Kind:** Public API · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** output/render-quality · **Lane:** video-render-colour · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

**Where:**

- `kiteplayer-output/src@apple/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/output/MetalVideoSupport.kt:440-452`
- `kiteplayer-output/src@apple/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/output/MetalVideoSupport.kt:529-531`
- `kiteplayer-output/src@android/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/output/AndroidGpuImageVideoRenderer.kt:1407-1415`
- `kiteplayer-output/src@android/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/output/AndroidGpuImageVideoRenderer.kt:1451`
- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/RenderQuality.kt:50-51`

**Evidence:** MetalVideoSupport.kt:440-452: `Debanding wins when both are asked for` and `if (deband) { rawY = kp_deband_plane(...) } else if (bicubic) { rawY = kp_bicubic(...) }`. MetalVideoSupport.kt:529: the linear-light second pass samples with the kernel only when `(q.flags & 4) != 0 && (q.flags & 2) == 0`, i.e. never while the deband bit is set, although debanding already ran in the first pass. AndroidGpuImageVideoRenderer.kt:1407-1415 and 1451: `if (uDebandThreshold > 0.0) {...} else if (uBicubic > 0.5) {...}`. RenderQuality.kt:50-51 documents `scaler` as `Which kernel resamples the picture when it is not drawn at its own size` with no exception.

**Claim:** A RenderQuality with deband = true and scaler = CatmullRom pays for debanding and gets bilinear scaling on Metal and on the Android GL tier. In the Metal linear-light path this is not even forced by a conflict: the first pass debands at source size and the second pass scales, so the kernel could run there and is skipped only to mirror the single-pass rule. On Android the kernel request also enlarges the intermediate buffer to the viewport (setRenderQuality KDoc), so memory is spent for an enlargement that is then done bilinearly.

**Scenario:** An app builds RenderQuality.Standard.copy(scaler = VideoScaler.CatmullRom) expecting the sharper upscale on a phone showing an 800p film; the picture is identical to Standard. On Android the queue's six buffers also grow to viewport size for nothing.

**Impact:** Misleading public API; a measurable waste on Android; the one combination most apps would reach for (Standard plus a better kernel) is the one that silently loses the kernel.

**Suggested fix:** Either state the exclusion in RenderQuality.scaler's KDoc and make isNeutral/validation reject or normalise the pair, or implement the combination: on Metal let kp_light_scale use the kernel regardless of the deband bit (the first pass already consumed it), and on Android run the deband ring on the bilinear centre and then the kernel, or deband into an intermediate before the blit.

**How to check it yourself:** Render a 480p test card through MetalFrameComposer with quality = RenderQuality(deband = true, scaler = CatmullRom) and with RenderQuality(deband = true) into a 1080p target and compare the pixels: they are identical. Repeat on the Android GL device test with uBicubic and uDebandThreshold both set.

**Verifier's note:** MetalVideoSupport.kt:438-446: `bool deband = (q.flags & 2) != 0; bool bicubic = (q.flags & 4) != 0 && q.lumaTexelX > 0.0;` then `if (deband) { rawY = kp_deband_plane(...) } else if (bicubic) { rawY = kp_bicubic(...) }` with the comment `Debanding wins when both are asked for`. Lines 519-531 (second linear-light pass): `Debanding ran in the first pass, and it still wins over the kernel ... so the two renderers treat every combination alike` and `float3 scaled = ((q.flags & 4) != 0 && (q.flags & 2) == 0) ? kp_bicubic(...) : light.sample(...)`. The flag assembly at lines 591-601 sets bit 2 for deband and bit 4 for CatmullRom independently, so both bits are set for the combination. AndroidGpuImageVideoRenderer.kt:1406-1412 shader comment `Debanding and the kernel are exclusive, and deband wins ... the combination stays open`, code `if (uDebandThreshold > 0.0) {...} else if (uBicubic > 0.5) {...}` (1414, 1451). The Android size law: line 492 `True runs the Catmull-Rom kernel AND lets the blit enlarge` and line 809 `val enlarge = bicubic.get() || ...`, so the enlargement is paid even when deband then suppresses the kernel. RenderQuality.kt:50-51 documents `scaler` as `Which kernel resamples the picture when it is not drawn at its own size.` and the VideoScaler.CatmullRom KDoc (lines 105-112) promises a sharper upscale with no exception; the deband KDoc (lines 29-41) mentions pairing with dither only. The exclusivity is stated only in shader comments, never in the public API. The one Metal composer test touching deband (MetalFrameComposerTest.kt:803) does not pair it with the kernel. Mechanism confirmed, no public documentation found.

### F-174 The spherical lens a renderer needs to implement projects() and setProjection() is in the spi package but marked internal API.

**Severity:** low (finder said medium, verifier corrected) · **Kind:** Public API · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** spi/spherical · **Lane:** design-capabilities-crossmatch · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

**Where:**

- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/spi/SphericalLens.kt:32-33`
- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/spi/SphericalLens.kt:114-115`
- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/spi/VideoRenderer.kt:1-327`

**Evidence:** SphericalLens.kt:32-33 `@KitePlayerInternalApi` / `public class SphericalLens(`; :114-115 `@KitePlayerInternalApi` / `public data class PicturePoint(...)`. VideoRenderer.kt declares `public fun projects(kind: ProjectionKind): Boolean = false` and `public fun setProjection(projection: VideoProjection?, view: SphericalView) {}` with no annotation. The lens KDoc at :28-31: "A renderer computes this once for each draw, on the processor, and hands [rotation], [scale], the centre and the bounds to its shader".

**Claim (as corrected by the verifier):** SphericalLens, the executable form of the 360 degree view law and the oracle the in-tree renderer tests use, is in the spi package but behind @KitePlayerInternalApi (level ERROR), so a third-party renderer that answers projects() = true must either reimplement the law from the prose in docs/spherical-video.md or opt into an API the annotation says is not for applications. docs/spherical-video.md:254-256 documents this status, so it is a known choice rather than an oversight.

**Finder's original claim:** The SPI invites a renderer to answer projects() = true, but the only piece of maths that makes a correct view (the lens the in-tree Compose, web and AWT renderers use) is opt-in internal, so an external renderer must either reimplement equirectangular and tiled projection maths from the SphericalView and VideoProjection types or take an unstable API dependency. Everything else a renderer needs in spi is public; this is the one exception, and it sits in the spi package.

**Scenario:** A third-party Vulkan renderer on Linux wants 360 degree support; its author finds SphericalLens in the spi package, uses it, and must add @OptIn(KitePlayerInternalApi::class) to a published library, which the annotation's own contract says is not for applications.

**Impact:** SPI cannot be implemented fully without internal API; third-party spherical rendering diverges from the engine's own.

**Suggested fix:** Make SphericalLens and PicturePoint public API with a stability note, or move them out of spi into an internal package so the boundary is honest.

**How to check it yourself:** grep -rn KitePlayerInternalApi kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/spi/ (only SphericalLens.kt:32 and :114), then read docs/spherical-video.md:238-256, which states the annotation and gives the law in prose.

**Verifier's note:** Facts verified. grep KitePlayerInternalApi over kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/spi/ hits only SphericalLens.kt:3 (import), :32 and :114. SphericalLens.kt:32-33 `@KitePlayerInternalApi` / `public class SphericalLens(`; :114-115 `@KitePlayerInternalApi` / `public data class PicturePoint(...)`. VideoRenderer.kt:135 `public fun projects(kind: ...): Boolean = false` and :145 `public fun setProjection(` carry no annotation. The annotation's KDoc (InternalApi.kt:6-9) says "Nothing behind this annotation is meant for an application", with opt-in level ERROR. Every in-tree renderer that projects uses the lens (kiteplayer-compose-video SphereView.*, WebGlVideoPass, kiteplayer-output AwtCanvasVideoRenderer and SphereViewRemap). Two things soften it: docs/spherical-video.md:238-256 spells the whole law out in prose (direction, rotation order, atan2 longitude and latitude, 0.5 + lon/360 across) and states plainly that SphericalLens is "in the core's spi package and behind KitePlayerInternalApi", so the status is a documented choice rather than an oversight, and a third party can implement from the prose. The finding's point stands that the only executable form of the law, and the oracle the in-tree tests compare against, is opt-in internal while sitting in the package meant for renderer authors. Severity lowered: documented, and 360 degree rendering by third-party renderers has no evidence of demand.

### F-058 A Compose app on Android has no library route to correct picture-in-picture parameters, because rotation reaches only the native view and the snapshot carries none

**Severity:** medium · **Kind:** Public API · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** view/android,pip · **Lane:** views-compose-ui-samples · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

**Where:**

- `kiteplayer-view/src@android/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/view/PictureInPictureEntry.kt:36-71`
- `kiteplayer-view/src@android/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/view/KitePlayerView.kt:398-423`
- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/PlayerState.kt:477-483`
- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/Tracks.kt:30-58`

**Evidence:** PictureInPictureEntry.kt 202-205: `public fun KitePlayerView.keepPictureInPictureParamsCurrent(activity: Activity, ...)`, an extension on the view only; 215-222 read `videoRotationDegrees`, which KitePlayerView.kt 399 defines as `internal val videoRotationDegrees: Int get() = videoRotation`, set only from the renderer callback `onVideoGeometry` (89-93, 569-581). PlayerState.kt 477-483: `public data class VideoSize(val width: Int, val height: Int, val pixelAspectNumerator: Int = 1, val pixelAspectDenominator: Int = 1)`; a grep for `rotation` in PlayerState.kt finds nothing. docs/module-contract.md 42: `KitePlayerSurface does not expose the view that it hosts`. In the pump, `PipUpdatePump.next` is called from a `Dispatchers.Default` collector (210-222) with a value the main thread writes (plain `var videoRotation`).

**Claim:** The aspect a PiP window needs is the displayed picture's, after the container rotation. That rotation is known only to the renderer, which tells KitePlayerView through a callback; the engine never publishes it in PlayerSnapshot or VideoSize. So `pictureInPictureParams()` and `keepPictureInPictureParamsCurrent()` can exist only on the view, and a Compose app using KitePlayerVideo (either path) must build `PictureInPictureParams` itself from `state.videoSize`, which for a phone recording with a 90 degree display matrix gives a landscape aspect for a portrait picture. The pump's cross-thread read of `videoRotation` is a second, smaller sign of the same fact: the value lives in the wrong place.

**Scenario:** Compose Android app, `KitePlayerVideo(player)` in a `ComponentActivity` with `supportsPictureInPicture`. The developer wants auto-enter on Android 12+, follows the view's PiP docs, and finds no API on the Compose side; they compute the aspect from `videoSize.displayWidth / height` and a vertically shot phone video opens a 16:9 window with the picture pillarboxed inside it.

**Impact:** Picture in picture, one of the README's headline features, is only fully supported through the XML view. The Compose entry point, which the module contract calls the recommended one, cannot do it correctly for rotated media.

**Suggested fix:** Add `rotationDegrees` (and the shown crop) to `PlayerSnapshot` (or to `VideoSize`) from the stream's display matrix at open, move `pictureInPictureAspect`/`PipUpdatePump` to read the snapshot, and offer a Compose-side helper (`rememberPictureInPictureParams(player)` or a `KitePlayer.pictureInPictureParams(autoEnter)` extension in kiteplayer) that KitePlayerView's version delegates to.

**How to check it yourself:** Grep kiteplayer-core for a rotation field in PlayerSnapshot/VideoSize (none), then try to write a PiP aspect for `testmedia`'s rotated90ccw.mp4 (the clip PictureInPictureTest carries) from `player.state.value.videoSize` alone.

**Verifier's note:** PictureInPictureEntry.kt is 71 lines, so the cited 202-237 is wrong; the code is 36-71: `public fun KitePlayerView.keepPictureInPictureParamsCurrent(activity: Activity, ...)` collects `player.state` on `CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.Default)` (44) and reads `rotationDegrees = videoRotationDegrees` (54), which KitePlayerView.kt 399 defines as `internal val videoRotationDegrees: Int get() = videoRotation`, a plain `private var videoRotation: Int = 0` (66) written on the main thread from `setVideoGeometry` (569-581), itself fed only by the renderer's `onVideoGeometry` callback (89-93). `pictureInPictureParams()` (408-423) is a member of the view. On the engine side `VideoSize` (PlayerState.kt 477-483) has width, height and pixel aspect only; `PlayerSnapshot.tracks` is `Tracks` whose `TrackInfo` (Tracks.kt 30-58) has `videoSize` and `frameRate` but no rotation; a grep for rotation in PlayerState.kt and Tracks.kt finds nothing. The only rotation in core's public types is `VideoTransform.rotationDegrees` (VideoTransform.kt 38), the user's own turn, and `CapturedFrame.rotationDegrees`, a frame capture. The container's rotation exists only in the SPI `PlayerStreamInfo.rotationDegrees` (MediaSource.kt 349-354) and in the renderer callback. kiteplayer-compose-video keeps `KiteVideoFrame` internal (KiteVideoRenderer.kt 36) and `KiteVideoState` exposes no rotation. A grep for PictureInPictureParams outside kiteplayer-view/src@android finds only the sample's MainActivity using the view extension. So a Compose app has no library route to the displayed aspect, as claimed. The cross-thread read is a visibility nit at worst (a stale Int until the next snapshot), which the finding already calls smaller.

### F-188 Network media on the web plays only in the worker, and the worker accepts no PlayerConfig, so the whole configuration surface is unreachable on the web.

**Severity:** low (finder said medium, verifier corrected) · **Kind:** Public API · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** web/parity · **Lane:** design-capabilities-crossmatch · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

**Where:**

- `kiteplayer/src@wasmJs/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/KitePlayerWorker.kt:57-70`
- `kiteplayer/src@wasmJs/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/WorkerRuntime.kt:72-77`
- `README.md:51`
- `README.md:163-166`

**Evidence:** KitePlayerWorker.kt:68 "- A `PlayerConfig`: the worker builds its player on the default one." and :64-67 listing `inspect`, `scanAudio`, `captureFrame`, `thumbnailAt`, recording, `memento`, `restore`, renderer attach, audio tap and `setExternalClock` as not crossing. WorkerRuntime.kt:72-77 `KitePlayer(defaults.copy(backends = ..., network = defaults.network.copy(ioResolver = SyncHttpResolver(defaults.buffer.stallTimeout))))`. README.md:51 `| **HLS and DASH** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | In a web worker |`; README.md:163-164 "A player on the page's main thread cannot play network media, because it cannot block while it waits for a read."

**Claim (as corrected by the verifier):** On wasmJs every http, HLS and DASH item needs KitePlayerWorker, and neither start() overload takes a PlayerConfig (the worker builds on PlayerConfig() at WorkerRuntime.kt:71-77). Per-item settings still cross as runtime setters (volume, HDR policy, flash guard, subtitle style, scale and position, equaliser, loop, shuffle) and a position resumes through MediaItem.startPosition, but construction-time policy does not: preferred audio and subtitle languages, BufferPolicy, volumeCeiling, ReplayGain, NetworkRecovery, SegmentStore, QueueConfig, hardware decode and deinterlace policy. The facade KDoc says so in one line; the README's web column and its "a few that its KDoc lists, such as recording" do not.

**Finder's original claim:** On wasmJs the main-thread player plays only bytes the page already holds; every http, HLS and DASH item needs KitePlayerWorker. The worker takes no PlayerConfig and no memento, so on the web an app cannot set preferred languages, subtitle style or scale defaults, buffer policy, volume ceiling, equaliser, ReplayGain, network recovery, segment store, queue behaviour, HDR policy seed or flash guard seed, and cannot resume a position. This is documented in KDoc but not in the README's platform table, which shows HLS and DASH as supported with one qualifier.

**Scenario:** A Compose Multiplatform app shares one `PlayerConfig { subtitles { preferredLanguages = listOf("ja") }; network { recovery = NetworkRecovery() } }` across targets. On Android it works. On the web the same code must route through KitePlayerWorker.start(canvas), the config is dropped on the floor, subtitles come up in the container default, and a Wi-Fi blip fails playback instead of reconnecting.

**Impact:** Platform parity hole on the one platform where every configuration default also cannot be changed after the fact; a shared-code app cannot behave the same on the web.

**Suggested fix:** Serialise PlayerConfig (all fields except backends, ioResolver, resampler, segmentStore and NetworkStatus, which hold objects) into the worker protocol and have WorkerRuntime build its player from it; add memento and restore to the protocol since they are already text (`PlayerMemento.asProperties()`). Add a "config and resume" row or footnote to the README table.

**How to check it yourself:** Read KitePlayerWorker.kt:620-652 (no PlayerConfig parameter) and WorkerRuntime.kt:71-77, then list the facade's public setters at KitePlayerWorker.kt:318-419 to see which settings do cross. Compare with PlayerConfig fields that have no setter: preferredLanguages, BufferPolicy, volumeCeiling, replayGain, recovery, segmentStore, QueueConfig.

**Verifier's note:** The core fact holds. KitePlayerWorker.kt:68 "- A `PlayerConfig`: the worker builds its player on the default one."; both start overloads (:620-625 and :646-652) take canvas, workerUrl, codecUrl, libassUrl and keepDisplayAwake, no PlayerConfig. WorkerRuntime.kt:71-77 `val defaults = PlayerConfig()` then `KitePlayer(defaults.copy(backends = ..., network = defaults.network.copy(ioResolver = SyncHttpResolver(defaults.buffer.stallTimeout))))`. README.md:51 shows HLS and DASH as "In a web worker" and README.md:163-168 says the worker "has the same calls and flows as KitePlayer, except for a few that its KDoc lists, such as recording", which understates a whole missing configuration surface. But the finding's list of what cannot be set is too long: the worker facade has runtime setters for most per-item settings, at KitePlayerWorker.kt:327 setVolume, :385 setHdrPolicy, :388 setFlashGuard, :394 setSubtitleScale, :397 setSubtitleStyle, :400 setSubtitlePosition, :416 setEqualizer, :357 setLoop, :360 setShuffle; and a position is resumed through MediaItem.startPosition (MediaItem.kt:79) even though memento/restore do not cross (:64). What truly cannot be reached on the worker is construction-time policy: SubtitleConfig/AudioConfig.preferredLanguages (PlayerConfig.kt:381), BufferPolicy, AudioConfig.volumeCeiling (:401) and replayGain (:413-417), NetworkConfig.recovery (:166) and segmentStore (:173), QueueConfig, hardwareDecode, deinterlace and the renderQuality default. The scenario's NetworkRecovery half is real; its subtitle-language half is real; its "subtitle style" implication is not, since setSubtitleStyle crosses. Documented in KDoc, so an API gap with a known shape rather than a hidden one.

## 11. KitePlayer: documentation that does not match the code

Each entry quotes the prose and the code it contradicts.

<!-- area: colour/docs -->

### F-102 Two colour comments describe code that no longer exists: the Metal tone map says the content peak is not plumbed, and the CPU converter says the GPU samples chroma nearest-neighbour.

**Severity:** low · **Kind:** Documentation · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** colour/docs · **Lane:** video-render-colour · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

**Where:**

- `kiteplayer-output/src@apple/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/output/MetalVideoSupport.kt:632-671`
- `kiteplayer-output/src@apple/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/output/MetalVideoSupport.kt:425-437`
- `kiteplayer-ffmpeg/src@native/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/ffmpeg/SoftwareConverter.native.kt:38-41`
- `kiteplayer-ffmpeg/src@native/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/ffmpeg/SoftwareConverter.native.kt:297-310`
- `kiteplayer-output/src@apple/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/output/MetalFrameComposer.kt:187`

**Evidence:** MetalVideoSupport.kt:636-638: `srcPeak is 1000 nits for both transfers: PQ mastering metadata ... is not plumbed through [ColorSpaceInfo] yet ... Recorded as the honest limit of this first tone-mapping pass.` while packToneUniforms at 653-672 takes `srcPeakNits: Float?` and MetalFrameComposer.encode passes `frame.toneMapPeakNits`. SoftwareConverter.native.kt:38-39: `Chroma upsampling here is nearest neighbour ... it is exactly what a GPU renderer does with a nearest-filtered texture, so the two can be compared pixel for pixel.` while MetalVideoSupport.kt:422 declares `constexpr sampler s(mag_filter::linear, min_filter::linear, ...)` and the shader adds the chroma siting offset from ChromaSampleOffset.kt.

**Claim (as corrected by the verifier):** Two colour comments are stale. MetalVideoSupport.kt:636-638 (an orphaned KDoc block) says the PQ content peak is not plumbed, while packToneUniforms takes srcPeakNits and MetalFrameComposer passes frame.toneMapPeakNits from scene and mastering metadata. SoftwareConverter.native.kt:38-41 and 304-309 say the CPU converter's nearest-neighbour chroma matches a nearest-filtered GPU texture pixel for pixel, while the Metal shader samples chroma bilinearly with a siting offset from chromaSampleOffset, so the two paths agree only approximately. No test compares the two paths pixel for pixel; ColourInstrumentTest judges Metal against an independent hand-written reference within a tolerance.

**Finder's original claim:** Both comments were true once and are now false. The first understates what the code does (the peak is plumbed from static and Dolby Vision metadata). The second overstates comparability: the GPU path samples chroma bilinearly with a half-texel siting shift, so GPU and CPU agree only within a tolerance, which is what ColourInstrumentTest in fact asserts.

**Scenario:** A maintainer reading either comment makes a decision on a false premise, for example skipping the peak plumbing as missing or treating a chroma fringe difference as a GPU bug.

**Impact:** Prose drifting from the tree is this project's stated failure mode.

**Suggested fix:** Rewrite the packToneUniforms KDoc to describe the peak source (toneMapPeakNits: scene, then title, then 1000) and the converter header to say the GPU is bilinear with siting while the CPU is nearest, and that the instrument compares within a tolerance.

**How to check it yourself:** Read MetalVideoSupport.kt:632-671 and MetalFrameComposer.kt:187,212,289 for the peak; read SoftwareConverter.native.kt:38-41 and 297-310 against MetalVideoSupport.kt:425 and 437.

**Verifier's note:** First comment: MetalVideoSupport.kt:636-638 reads `srcPeak is 1000 nits for both transfers: PQ mastering metadata (SMPTE ST 2086 / CTA-861.3) is not plumbed through [ColorSpaceInfo] yet ... Recorded as the honest limit of this first tone-mapping pass.` It is now an orphaned KDoc block sitting directly above the KDoc of `willToneMap` (640-647), and `packToneUniforms` (652-671) takes `srcPeakNits: Float? = null` and uses it at 667 `if (mode == 1) srcPeakNits ?: 1000f else 1000f`. MetalFrameComposer.kt passes `frame.toneMapPeakNits` at lines 187, 212 and 289, and VideoFrame.kt:399-409 derives it from `sceneMaxNits` and `hdr?.peakNits`. So the comment is stale. Second comment: SoftwareConverter.native.kt:38-39 says nearest neighbour `is exactly what a GPU renderer does with a nearest-filtered texture, so the two can be compared pixel for pixel`, and the same claim is repeated in the chromaSampleShift KDoc at 304-309 (`a nearest-filtered GPU texture, which this converter exists to be comparable with, samples chroma texel x / 2 whatever the metadata says`). The project's Metal shader does the opposite: MetalVideoSupport.kt:425 `constexpr sampler s(mag_filter::linear, min_filter::linear, address::clamp_to_edge);` and 437 `float2 chromaCoord = in.texcoord + float2(c.chromaOffsetX, c.chromaOffsetY);` fed from `chromaSampleOffset(...)` at MetalFrameComposer.kt:636 and 734. One correction to the finding: ColourInstrumentTest.kt:38-39 judges Metal output `against an INDEPENDENT reference (the coefficients are written here by hand ...)` within TOLERANCE, not against SoftwareConverter, so the test does not assert GPU-vs-CPU agreement; MetalFrameComposerTest.kt:182 only shares `The same arithmetic as the shader and SoftwareConverter` for expected values. The substance of the docs finding holds.

<!-- area: compose-ui -->

### F-105 onRendererAttached fires when no renderer was attached

**Severity:** low · **Kind:** Documentation · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** compose-ui · **Lane:** views-compose-ui-samples · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

**Where:**

- `kiteplayer-compose-ui/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/compose/KitePlayerVideo.kt:39-44`
- `kiteplayer-compose-ui/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/compose/KitePlayerVideo.kt:158-165`
- `kiteplayer-compose-ui/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/compose/KitePlayerVideo.kt:216-227`
- `kiteplayer-view/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/view/PlayerViewBinding.kt:112-116`
- `kiteplayer-view/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/view/MissingRendererNotice.kt:6-20`

**Evidence:** KDoc 39-40: `[onRendererAttached] fires once this composable's video output is attached to [player]: the native view attaches as soon as the player is set`. NativeViewVideo 163-164: `LaunchedEffect(player) { player?.let { currentOnAttached(it) } }`, with no knowledge of whether the view built or attached anything. PlayerViewBinding 112-115: when `refusesAttach(attachFailure)` the binding logs `the view shows nothing, because its player refused the renderer` and returns; MissingRendererNotice.kt 287-296: a view with no factory logs and attaches nothing.

**Claim:** On the native view path the callback is `player was set`, not `renderer attached`. A closed player (refused attach, #603) or a view without a renderer factory still produces the callback. The canvas path is honest: it reports only after `attachRenderer` returned without throwing (221-226).

**Scenario:** An app latches `onRendererAttached` to start playback or to hide a placeholder; with a player closed by another screen the callback fires, the placeholder goes, and the picture never comes.

**Impact:** Wrong signal in an edge case; a caller cannot distinguish the two paths' semantics.

**Suggested fix:** Either reword the KDoc (`fires once the player is handed to the output`), or thread an `onAttached` hook from PlayerViewBinding through the views (a `rendererAttached` callback property) and fire the Compose report from it.

**How to check it yourself:** No device needed: in a JVM ImageComposeScene, as RendererAttachedReportTest does, create a stub-backend player, call `player.close()`, then compose `NativeViewVideo(player, Modifier, surface = { _, m -> Box(m) }) { reported += it }` and render once; `reported` holds the closed player although nothing could attach. The canvas path's LaunchedEffect (lines 221-226) returns before the callback in the same situation.

**Verifier's note:** KDoc lines 39-40: `[onRendererAttached] fires once this composable's video output is attached to [player]: the native view attaches as soon as the player is set`. NativeViewVideo lines 163-165: `LaunchedEffect(player) { player?.let { currentOnAttached(it) } }` with no reading of whether a renderer exists. PlayerViewBinding.kt lines 112-115: on `refusesAttach(attachFailure)` it logs `the view shows nothing, because its player refused the renderer` and returns, leaving `renderer = null`; nothing reaches the Compose layer. MissingRendererNotice.kt (23 lines, not 287-296) line 18 logs `has a player and no renderer factory, so it shows no picture`. The canvas path (lines 221-226) returns from the LaunchedEffect on a refused attach before calling `currentOnRendererAttached`, so the two paths disagree and the docs describe the honest one. Low docs finding, holds.

### F-031 BufferPolicy.totalBytes is documented as the stall point but the engine reads on to twice it, and with the byte cache the real per-player ceiling is about 96 MiB.

**Severity:** medium · **Kind:** Documentation · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** core/memory-budget · **Lane:** design-capabilities-crossmatch · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

**Where:**

- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/PlayerConfig.kt:252-254`
- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/PlayerConfig.kt:226-228`
- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/internal/PlaybackCore.kt:14146-14154`
- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/internal/PlaybackCore.kt:14204`

**Evidence:** PlayerConfig.kt:252 `/** The demux worker stalls when the total across all streams reaches either of these. */` over `val totalBytes: Long = 32L * 1024 * 1024`. PlayerConfig.kt:226-228 `backWindowBytes: Long = 8L * 1024 * 1024`, `forwardWindowBytes: Long = 32L * 1024 * 1024`. PlaybackCore.kt:14154 `return bytes >= config.buffer.totalBytes || longest >= config.buffer.totalDuration.inWholeMicroseconds` and :14204 `if (behindUs < INTERLEAVE_REACH_US && held < 2 * config.buffer.totalBytes) return Relief.ReadOn`.

**Claim (as corrected by the verifier):** BufferPolicy.totalBytes's KDoc says the demux worker stalls at it, but relieveInterleaving (#570, by design) keeps reading for a stream that gave a packet within the last 10 s until twice totalBytes is held, and the byte cache (IoCachePolicy.forwardWindowBytes, 32 MiB by default) is a separate budget on every reader-fed open that neither KDoc relates to the other. With the defaults a network open can hold up to 64 MiB of packets plus 32 MiB of cache, and lowering one budget does not touch the other.

**Finder's original claim:** The totalBytes KDoc describes a hard stop. relieveInterleaving (#570) deliberately keeps reading past the budget for a stream that recently gave packets, until twice the byte budget is held. The IoCachePolicy window is a second 32 MiB of RAM on every MediaIo-fed open. So the defaults allow 64 MiB of packets plus 32 MiB of cache for one player, which an app sizing a two-player picture-in-picture screen on a 2 GB phone cannot read from the config docs. The two budgets are also not aware of each other: lowering totalBytes for a small device does nothing to the cache and vice versa.

**Scenario:** An Android TV stick with 1 GB (#64) plays a poorly interleaved MKV over the network: packets reach 64 MiB, the cache 32 MiB, plus decoded frames; the app that set `buffer { totalBytes = 16 MiB }` believing that capped RAM still sees 64 MiB.

**Impact:** Untrue KDoc on a sizing knob; no single number an integrator can budget against; two independent 32 MiB defaults on every platform including low-memory ones.

**Suggested fix:** State the 2x relief ceiling in totalBytes' KDoc, or make the relief ceiling a multiplier the policy owns. Consider one `MemoryBudget` that derives both totalBytes and forwardWindowBytes, and lower the web and TV defaults.

**How to check it yourself:** Read PlaybackCore.kt:14185-14205 against PlayerConfig.kt:252 and :216-229. Then read CachingMediaIo.kt:26-28, which already states the two budgets are independent. For a live proof, use the scripted backend with a two-stream script whose second stream stops for under 10 s while the first keeps coming after the first stream's queue is already over totalBytes and the second is under readyDuration; assert allPacketQueues.sumOf { bytesBuffered } exceeds totalBytes and stays under 2 * totalBytes.

**Verifier's note:** Evidence holds at the cited lines. PlayerConfig.kt:252-253: `/** The demux worker stalls when the total across all streams reaches either of these. */` over `val totalBytes: Long = 32L * 1024 * 1024`. PlaybackCore.kt:14154: `return bytes >= config.buffer.totalBytes || longest >= ...` is the budget, and relieveInterleaving at :14204 reads `if (behindUs < INTERLEAVE_REACH_US && held < 2 * config.buffer.totalBytes) return Relief.ReadOn`, with the KDoc at :14189-14192 saying in words: "The reads go on past the budget for such a stream, until [INTERLEAVE_REACH_US] of the others was read with nothing of it, or twice the byte budget is held." INTERLEAVE_REACH_US = 10_000_000L (:16197). The byte cache is separate: PlaybackCore.kt:4189-4190 `val cachingIo = if (watchedIo != null && config.network.ioCache.enabled) { CachingMediaIo(watchedIo, config.network.ioCache) }`, and CachingMediaIo's own KDoc (:26-28) says the packet queues above "already read ahead by BufferPolicy's budgets", so the two budgets are known to be independent and neither KDoc tells the app so. No doc under docs/ or README mentions RAM for either. CLAUDE.md records the 2x read-on as a deliberate #570 invariant, so the engine behaviour is right; what is wrong is the totalBytes KDoc calling it a stall point. Two narrowings: the 2x applies only in the #570 case (some selected queue held under readiness while a stream that gave packets within the last 10 s of reads sits empty), and the cache applies only to reader-fed opens (an item with its own MediaIo, or a URI the network resolver answers), not to an open through the backend's own protocols.

### F-126 The renderer contract says a refused frame is counted as a drop; the schedule counts it as a refusal and documents that it deliberately does not count it as a drop.

**Severity:** low · **Kind:** Documentation · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** core/spi-docs · **Lane:** video-render-colour · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

**Where:**

- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/spi/VideoRenderer.kt:64-70`
- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/VideoPlayback.kt:209-226`

**Evidence:** VideoRenderer.kt:67-68 on present(): `@return false when the frame was not presented ... The engine counts that as a drop.` VideoPlayback.kt:212: `A renderer refusal is [refusedFrames] and is deliberately not counted here.` with `public val droppedFrames: Long get() = droppedLate` at 217 and `public val refusedFrames: Long get() = refused` at 226. Rule 5 at VideoRenderer.kt:24-25 also says lost-surface frames `are counted as dropped`.

**Claim:** Two public documents contradict each other on what a false return means for the diagnostics. The schedule's reading is the one the code implements.

**Scenario:** An SPI implementer or an app reading droppedFrames to detect a slow pipeline follows the SPI text and misreads a dead surface as a decoder problem, which is exactly the confusion the VideoPlayback KDoc says the split was made to avoid.

**Impact:** Misleading documentation on a public interface.

**Suggested fix:** Change VideoRenderer.present's return KDoc and rule 5 to say the frame is counted as refused (refusedFrames), not dropped.

**How to check it yourself:** Read the two KDoc passages side by side; run the engine with a renderer whose present returns false and compare droppedFrames and refusedFrames.

**Verifier's note:** All three quoted passages exist as cited. VideoRenderer.kt:24-25 rule 5: `Playback continues, video frames are counted as dropped, and audio keeps playing`. VideoRenderer.kt:67-68 on present(): `@return false when the frame was not presented, for example because the surface is gone. The engine counts that as a drop.` VideoPlayback.kt:212: `A renderer refusal is [refusedFrames] and is deliberately not counted here.` with `public val droppedFrames: Long get() = droppedLate` (217) and `public val refusedFrames: Long get() = refused` (226). The code agrees with VideoPlayback: at VideoPlayback.kt:505-510 `if (renderer.present(frame, targetNanos)) { submitted++ ... } else { refused++ }`, and `droppedLate++` is only at line 393 on the late path. PlayerState.kt:366 on PlaybackStats.refusedFrames even says `Counted apart from [droppedFramesLate], which it used to be folded into.` So the SPI KDoc describes the old folding and the public stats describe the split. No guard or later correction found in the SPI file.

### F-130 Several working-notes claims about tests and sizes no longer match the tree

**Severity:** low · **Kind:** Documentation · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** docs · **Lane:** build-distribution-tests-ci · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

**Where:**

- `CLAUDE.md:130-133`
- `CLAUDE.md:89`
- `README.md:504-505`
- `CONTRIBUTING.md:122`
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:1201-1203`
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:113`
- `scripts/web-tests/browser.mjs:19`
- `scripts/check-web-size.sh:70-75`

**Evidence:** CLAUDE.md:131-132: `the test runner's per-test default is 2000 ms and Kotlin does not raise it. Every module that runs browser tests needs a timeout config file; copy the one that has it.` `find . -name 'karma*' -o -name '*.conf.js' -o -name 'mocha*'` finds nothing, and browser.mjs:19 has one global `timeoutMinutes: 45` and no per-test timeout. CLAUDE.md:89: `The five Actions secrets are set`; publish.yml:48-50 lists four and says `SIGNING_IN_MEMORY_KEY_ID is no longer read`. README.md:504: `0.7 MB for the worker player`; check-web-size.sh:70-75 says the worker measured `891,876` bytes gzipped against a budget of `901775` (0.86 MiB). CONTRIBUTING.md:122: `Tier 2, roughly 10 to 15 minutes`, while tier 2 includes `kotlin publish mavenLocal --non-transitive` of all 18 modules for every platform (check-gate.sh:92-101) and ci.yml:94-97 records the ratchets alone at `from 12 minutes to 2 h 18` on a cold cache.

**Claim:** Four statements a contributor acts on are stale: the browser per-test timeout gotcha describes a runner that was replaced (a hung browser test now blocks for 45 minutes instead of being killed at two seconds, which is a different trap), the secret count is wrong, the README's worker size is about a quarter under the measured figure, and the tier-2 duration is off by an order of magnitude on a cold machine.

**Scenario:** A contributor adds a browser test that awaits a promise that never resolves; expecting the two-second kill, they read the 45-minute stall as a hang in the engine. A reader budgets 15 minutes for tier 2 and kills it half way.

**Impact:** Time lost and misdiagnosis; the notes file whose rule is `delete a line when it stops being true` has lines that stopped being true.

**Suggested fix:** Rewrite the browser timeout gotcha to describe browser.mjs (one global 45-minute limit, no per-test kill) or add a per-test timeout to harness.mjs; change `five` to `four`; update the README worker size from check-web-size.sh's last measurement; replace the tier-2 estimate with `tens of minutes warm, hours cold`.

**How to check it yourself:** `find . \( -name 'karma*' -o -name '*.conf.js' -o -name 'mocha*' \) -not -path '*/build/*'` (nothing); `sed -n 1201,1203p .github/workflows/ci.yml`; `grep -n 'secrets\.' .github/workflows/publish.yml | sort -u` (four); `sed -n 70,75p scripts/check-web-size.sh`; `sed -n 175,176p scripts/check-gate.sh` and `sed -n 113p .github/workflows/ci.yml`.

**Verifier's note:** Browser timeout: CLAUDE.md:130-133 reads `A browser test that runs longer than two seconds is killed rather than failed, because the test runner's per-test default is 2000 ms and Kotlin does not raise it. Every module that runs browser tests needs a timeout config file; copy the one that has it.` No karma, mocha or `karma.config.d` file exists outside build/ (`find` returns nothing). ci.yml:1201-1203 says the opposite of the gotcha: `./kotlin test -p wasmJs gives a module 30 seconds in the browser, so scripts/web-tests runs the browser half instead`, and browser.mjs:19 has only `timeoutMinutes: 45` with the whole-run timer at 254-258; harness.mjs and run.py mention no timeout. Secrets: CLAUDE.md:89 `The five Actions secrets are set`; publish.yml:44-47 lists MAVEN_CENTRAL_USERNAME, MAVEN_CENTRAL_PASSWORD, SIGNING_IN_MEMORY_KEY, SIGNING_IN_MEMORY_KEY_PASSWORD and says `SIGNING_IN_MEMORY_KEY_ID is no longer read`; `grep secrets\.` finds exactly those four. Worker size: README.md:504-505 `0.7 MB for the worker player`; check-web-size.sh:70-75 `The worker budget is now 0.86 MiB` and `The worker grew ... to 891,876`. Tier 2: CONTRIBUTING.md:122 `### Tier 2, roughly 10 to 15 minutes`; check-gate.sh:175-176 lists tier2 steps `fixtures base build_logic publication macos ios_simulator android_host c_sanitizers jvm web linux windows cross_compile sample`, where `publication` (lines 92-101) runs `kotlin publish mavenLocal --non-transitive` for every published module. The `2 h 18` quote is at ci.yml:113, not 94-97: `A cold cache has since made the ratchets alone take from 12 minutes to 2 h 18`. The duration part is judgement with no local measurement, but the step list and the CI note support it.

### F-131 The dispatcher documentation counts eight lanes but SharedLaneDispatchers has nine

**Severity:** low · **Kind:** Documentation · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** docs · **Lane:** engine-actor-open · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/internal/PlatformDispatchers.kt:79-80`

**Evidence:** KDoc: 'Eight SERIAL LANES over the runtime's shared pools instead of eight owned OS threads: the session actor, the video scheduler, demux, video decode, audio decode, audio feed, subtitle raster and release.' (27-30). The class also declares `override val parse: CoroutineContext = calm.limitedParallelism(1)` (78-80), added for #594.

**Claim:** The parse lane was added after the comment was written; the count and the list are stale.

**Scenario:** A reader of the doc counting lanes for thread budgeting gets eight.

**Impact:** Misleading documentation only.

**Suggested fix:** Say nine and add 'external subtitle parse' to the list.

**Verifier's note:** PlatformDispatchers.kt lines 27-30 read: ` * Eight SERIAL LANES over the runtime's shared pools instead of eight owned OS threads: the session` / ` * actor, the video scheduler, demux, video decode, audio decode, audio feed, subtitle raster and` / ` * release.` Line 44 repeats the count: ` * one of these eight: the platform output owns it, and the ring is all it touches.` The class body overrides nine contexts: session, videoSchedule, demux, videoDecode, audioDecode, audioFeed, raster, release and, at line 80, `override val parse: CoroutineContext = calm.limitedParallelism(1)` under the comment `// Computation, and serial, so two files parse one after the other and never on the actor.` The parse lane is declared on the interface in PlaybackWorkers.kt 60-67 with the KDoc 'Where an external subtitle file is decoded and parsed, off the actor, whose lane a large file otherwise held for up to a second (#594)', so it was added after the eight-lane text, which never gained the ninth. ### F-132 The rendering document reports flash capture results for 24 drawings while the catalogue it describes has 15

**Severity:** low · **Kind:** Documentation · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** docs · **Lane:** audioviz · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

**Where:**

- `docs/audioviz-rendering-api.md:54`
- `docs/audioviz-rendering-api.md:556-560`

**Evidence:** docs/audioviz-rendering-api.md 46-47: 'The catalogue has 15 drawings on desktop, iOS and Android 13 and newer. On older Android it has 12'. Lines 556-560: 'The capture test ran on all 24 drawings on 2026-09-29, and none of them crosses the policy in the captured output. Bars, Fracture, Iris and Odyssey reach three on the drum loop, the limit itself, and the other twenty stay below it. With reduced motion on, every drawing stays inside the policy. Pipe and Honeycomb still flash once in their busiest second, and the other twenty-two flash not at all.' VizCatalog.kt 31-48 lists 15 drawings.

**Claim (as corrected by the verifier):** The flash verdicts in docs/audioviz-rendering-api.md 556-560 describe a 24-drawing catalogue measured on 2026-09-29; nine drawings were retired on 2026-10-12 and the shipped catalogue has 15 (line 54 of the same document says so). The per-drawing counts ('the other twenty', 'twenty-two') cannot be true of the shipped set. FlashCaptureTest still asserts the policy on the current catalogue, but only when someone runs './scripts/audioviz-tests.sh survey'; CI runs only 'gate', which excludes it, so the document carries no measurement of the shipped drawings.

**Finder's original claim:** The flash verdicts quoted as the measured state of the catalogue were taken on an older 24-drawing catalogue; nine drawings were removed and the remaining ones have changed since (Bars, Honeycomb, Iris and others were rewritten into their current forms). The sentence 'none of them crosses the policy' is therefore not a statement about the shipped drawings.

**Scenario:** A reader of the document, or a reviewer of the photosensitivity claim, takes the 2026-09-29 result as the current measurement of the 15 shipped drawings.

**Impact:** A safety claim in the public docs that no longer describes the code; the fix is a rerun of the survey and an updated paragraph.

**Suggested fix:** Run `scripts/audioviz-tests.sh survey` on the current catalogue, replace the paragraph with the new per-drawing counts and date, and either state which drawings sit at the limit now or remove the stale names.

**How to check it yourself:** Count the constructors in VizCatalog.create() (kiteplayer-audioviz/src/.../viz/VizCatalog.kt 31-47, 15), read docs/audioviz-rendering-api.md 54 and 556-560, and run 'git log --format=%ad --date=short -S retire -- kiteplayer-audioviz/src' to see the 2026-10-12 retirements after the quoted 2026-09-29 date. To refresh the numbers, run './scripts/audioviz-tests.sh survey' and read the FlashCaptureTest output lines ('flashes in the busiest second, fast fixture then drum loop').

**Verifier's note:** docs/audioviz-rendering-api.md line 54 (not 46-47) reads 'The catalogue has 15 drawings on desktop, iOS and Android 13 and newer. On older Android it has 12,' and lines 556-560 read 'The capture test ran on all 24 drawings on 2026-09-29, and none of them crosses the policy in the captured output. Bars, Fracture, Iris and Odyssey reach three on the drum loop, the limit itself, and the other twenty stay below it. ... Pipe and Honeycomb still flash once in their busiest second, and the other twenty-two flash not at all.' VizCatalog.kt 31-47 lists exactly 15 constructors (Bars, OceanMist, TwinBloom, Contour, Alchemy, Pipe, ThinIce, Glitch, Odyssey, NeonLoFi, Silk, Lines, Honeycomb, Fracture, Iris) before '.filter { it.canRunHere() }'. Git history shows drawings retired after the quoted date: '7164565 2026-10-12 retire kaleidoscope and wavy spiral now that iris carries them', '4464919 2026-10-12 retire fluctus now that silk carries its stage', '6353855 2026-10-12 retire threads now that fracture carries its dust'. So the 24-drawing verdicts predate the shipped catalogue. One nuance the finding leaves out: FlashCaptureTest (test@jvm/.../FlashCaptureTest.kt line 38) iterates 'VizCatalog.create()' and asserts the policy, so the policy itself is still checked against the shipped 15 whenever the survey runs; but it is in the RENDERING_SUITES set of scripts/audioviz-tests.sh, which 'gate' excludes, and ci.yml line 346 runs only 'gate'. So nothing automated has re-measured since, and no newer numbers appear anywhere in docs/ (grep for the counts finds only these lines). Docs finding stands.

### F-133 Four pieces of audio documentation describe behaviour the code no longer has: mono/stereo-only sinks, a pipeline gain stage, and a real-time thread that spins on the feeder

**Severity:** low · **Kind:** Documentation · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** docs/audio · **Lane:** audio-clock-ring-sinks · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

**Where:**

- `kiteplayer-output/src@android/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/output/AudioTrackSink.kt:32-33`
- `kiteplayer-output/src@jvm/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/output/DesktopAudioSink.kt:35`
- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/AudioPlayback.kt:975-976`
- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/spi/AudioSink.kt:203-207`
- `kiteplayer-core/src@native/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/internal/NativeAudioRing.kt:131-137`

**Evidence:** AudioTrackSink.kt:32 "The sink accepts mono or stereo only and never converts" versus :171-174 `channels = when (request.channels) { 1, 2, 6, 8 -> request.channels; else -> 2 }` (and the test at AudioTrackSinkTest.kt:182 is still named `open negotiates mono or stereo`). DesktopAudioSink.kt:35 "The sink accepts mono or stereo and never converts" versus :156-161 which asks the mixer and keeps 6 or 8. AudioPlayback.kt:975-976 "applied by the pipeline's gain stage as one multiply per sample with a short ramp" versus pushGain :1145-1164, which writes the gain into the ring (`ring?.setGain(ringGain)`) and the device (`sink.setDeviceGain(deviceGain)`); the same KDoc at :518-520 correctly says it moved. AudioSink.kt:204-208 says of KotlinAudioRing "while publishing the clock anchor, the real-time thread reads a sequence counter the feeder writes, and it retries with no bound if it catches the feeder mid-update" versus KotlinAudioRing.kt:39-46 and :754-779, where each slot has its own counter, the walk is `each slot tried once`, and a torn slot ends it (`torn = true; break`).

**Claim:** Each sentence was true at some point and is now false. The AudioSink SPI one matters most because it is public documentation that tells a sink author the portable ring has a priority inversion the code fixed (#221).

**Scenario:** A reader of the public SPI or the sink classes draws wrong conclusions about channel support and about which ring is safe on a real-time thread.

**Impact:** Misleading public documentation; no runtime effect.

**Suggested fix:** Update the four passages: both sinks take 1, 2, 6 and 8 channels (desktop when the mixer agrees); the volume lives in the ring and, where the sink answers setDeviceGain, in the device; the Kotlin ring's real-time side never retries, while its non-real-time anchor reader is the one that still spins (see the next finding).

**How to check it yourself:** Read the cited lines side by side.

**Verifier's note:** All four stale sentences exist and are contradicted by the code beside them. AudioTrackSink.kt:32 "The sink accepts mono or stereo only and never converts" against :171-174 `channels = when (request.channels) { 1, 2, 6, 8 -> request.channels; else -> 2 }`, and the test is still named `open negotiates mono or stereo and fails invalid requests before device creation` (AudioTrackSinkTest.kt:182). DesktopAudioSink.kt:35 "The sink accepts mono or stereo and never converts" against :156-161, which asks `driverFactory.supports(...)` and keeps `wanted` when the mixer says yes. AudioPlayback.kt:975-976 "applied by the pipeline's gain stage as one multiply per sample with a short ramp" against pushGain :1145-1156 `ring?.setGain(ringGain)` and `sink.setDeviceGain(deviceGain)`, while :518-520 already says "The gain is NOT picked up here any more. It moved to the ring's read side". AudioSink.kt:204-206 "while publishing the clock anchor, the real-time thread reads a sequence counter the feeder writes, and it retries with no bound if it catches the feeder mid-update" against KotlinAudioRing.kt:41-46 "Each timestamp segment has its own sequence counter, [publishAnchor] walks the segments at most once, and a slot that the feeder is changing ends the walk" and the code at :754-762 `if (opening % 2L != 0L) { torn = true; break }`. A fifth instance the finding could add: NativeAudioRing.kt:134-135 still says the Kotlin ring "answers the same situation by spinning without a bound" and has no counterpart counter, while KotlinAudioRing has `segmentGiveupCount` (:787) and `segmentGiveups`.

### F-038 The cancellation design doc still says a URL-fallback open cannot be stopped, but the backend already interrupts it

**Severity:** medium · **Kind:** Documentation · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** docs/cancellation · **Lane:** public-api-and-docs · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

**Where:**

- `docs/cancellation-and-bounded-waits.md:53-55`
- `docs/cancellation-and-bounded-waits.md:257`
- `kiteplayer-ffmpeg/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/ffmpeg/ItemSources.kt:63-66`
- `kiteplayer-ffmpeg/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/ffmpeg/ItemSources.kt:96`
- `kiteplayer-ffmpeg/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/ffmpeg/ItemSources.kt:293-295`

**Evidence:** Doc 53-55: "An open through the URL fallback cannot be stopped yet. The fix needs an interrupt that exists before the open returns, which is yuroyami/KiteFFmpeg#62. Until then a stop waits for such an open to end". Doc 257: "It cannot be stopped during the open until yuroyami/KiteFFmpeg#62." ItemSources.kt 63-66: "Cancelling the calling coroutine ends the open ... The cancel raises an [OpenInterrupt], which FFmpeg sees inside its network protocols and during stream discovery"; 96: `val cancel = OpenInterrupt()`; 293-295: `private fun openUrlFallback(uri, formatHint, options, cancel: OpenInterrupt): MediaSource = MediaSource.open(fallbackAddress(uri), urlFallbackOptions(...), cancel)`. KiteFFmpeg CHANGELOG 821: "An open you can interrupt. Pass an OpenInterrupt to MediaSource.open and call interrupt() from another thread". KiteFFmpeg#62 is not among the open issues listed for the audit.

**Claim:** The limitation the design document records twice has been lifted: KiteFFmpeg ships OpenInterrupt and KitePlayer's URL fallback passes one, so a stop or a cancelled open() reaches FFmpeg's network protocols. The document, which the KDoc of BufferPolicy and NetworkRecovery points readers to, now describes a weaker guarantee than the code gives and cites a closed issue as pending.

**Scenario:** A developer evaluating whether a stuck http:// open can be cancelled reads the page, concludes it cannot, and adds their own watchdog or avoids the fallback; or a maintainer trusts the page and reintroduces an uninterruptible path believing nothing depended on it.

**Impact:** Misleading design documentation for a safety property the owner considers load bearing (the same page says "Check this reasoning again before you change the bridge, the open or the teardown").

**Suggested fix:** Rewrite lines 53-55 and 257 to say the URL fallback open is interrupted through OpenInterrupt inside FFmpeg's protocol loop and stream discovery, with the remaining gap (a wait anywhere else inside FFmpeg finishes first, per ItemSources.kt 66), and remove the #62 references. Check lines 56-57 about HLS child contexts against KiteFFmpeg's patch list (no interrupt patch exists among 0001-0015) and keep or drop accordingly.

**How to check it yourself:** Read ItemSources.kt 58-100 and 288-296; on the JVM open an http:// address on a server that accepts the connection and never answers, call stop() after one second, and observe the open ends promptly rather than after the 10 s read timeout.

**Verifier's note:** docs/cancellation-and-bounded-waits.md 53-55 reads 'An open through the URL fallback cannot be stopped yet. The fix needs an interrupt that exists before the open returns, which is yuroyami/KiteFFmpeg#62. Until then a stop waits for such an open to end', and 257 'It cannot be stopped during the open until yuroyami/KiteFFmpeg#62.' The code contradicts both. ItemSources.kt 96 `val cancel = OpenInterrupt()`; 180 `val source = openCancellably(cancel::interrupt) { openUrlFallback(item.uri, item.formatHint, options, cancel) }`; 293-295 `MediaSource.open(fallbackAddress(uri), urlFallbackOptions(uri, options, formatHint), cancel)`; and 206-212 `interruptedWhenCancelled` registers `link.invokeOnCompletion { cause -> if (cause != null) interrupt() }` so the coroutine's cancellation raises the interrupt during the blocking open. The fallback's own KDoc at 290 says '[cancel] stops the open while it waits on the network.' On the KiteFFmpeg side, OpenInterrupt.kt 25-27 states FFmpeg 'checks for it inside its network protocols and during stream discovery', CHANGELOG 821 announces 'An open you can interrupt', and `gh api repos/yuroyami/KiteFFmpeg/issues/62` reports state 'closed' on 2026-09-25 with the title 'An open cannot be interrupted, because interrupt() needs the source it returns'. PlayerConfig.kt 164 points readers to this document. The adjacent bullet at 56-57 about the HLS demuxer not copying the interrupt callback to child contexts is a separate statement the finding does not contest, and no patch under KiteFFmpeg/native/patches/ffmpeg addresses it, so only the two URL-fallback sentences are stale.

### F-039 The README's iOS static framework linker flags are KiteFFmpeg's list and omit what libass needs, and the iOS sample cannot catch it

**Severity:** medium · **Kind:** Documentation · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** docs/ios · **Lane:** build-distribution-tests-ci · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** medium

**Where:**

- `README.md:108-114`
- `kiteplayer-libass/native/libass.def:20-21`
- `kiteplayer-rt/native/kitert.def:34-35`
- `kiteplayer-sample-ios/module.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:138`

**Evidence:** README.md:113: `-ObjC -lz -framework CoreFoundation -framework CoreMedia -framework CoreVideo -framework VideoToolbox -framework AudioToolbox`, which is exactly KiteFFmpeg's `linkerOpts.ios = -lz -framework CoreFoundation -framework CoreMedia -framework CoreVideo -framework VideoToolbox -framework AudioToolbox` (KiteFFmpeg kiteffmpeg/interop/ffmpeg.def:30). libass.def:21: `linkerOpts.ios = -lz -liconv -lc++ -framework CoreText -framework CoreFoundation -framework CoreGraphics`. kiteplayer/module.yaml lists `//kiteplayer-libass: exported` for every platform. The iOS sample's pbxproj line 138 runs `"${KOTLIN_CLI_WRAPPER_PATH}" tool xcode-integration`, the toolchain's own link step, and a grep for OTHER_LDFLAGS in the pbxproj finds nothing, so the sample never exercises a hand-written flag list.

**Claim:** A Gradle consumer that sets `isStatic = true` must repeat every cinterop linkerOpts of every klib in the framework in Xcode, because Kotlin embeds them only for a dynamic framework. The README gives the FFmpeg half and leaves out the libass half: `-liconv`, `-lc++` (HarfBuzz is C++), `-framework CoreText` and `-framework CoreGraphics`. A pure Swift app does not link libc++ or libiconv on its own. The result is an Xcode link failure with undefined symbols from HarfBuzz and libass, which the README says it prevents.

**Scenario:** A developer adds `implementation("io.github.yuroyami:kiteplayer:0.3.0")`, builds a static framework for a Swift app, pastes the README flags, and the archive fails with `Undefined symbols: _iconv_open, std::__1::..., _CTFontCreateWithName` from libkiteass.a objects. The KitePlayer sample is green in CI because the toolchain links it.

**Impact:** The most common iOS integration path fails at first install for anyone who follows the README literally, and the project's one iOS build in CI structurally cannot detect it.

**Suggested fix:** Extend the README list with the libass.def iOS flags (and state that kitert's AudioToolbox and kitemetal's Metal are covered or add them). Better, generate the list: a small script that concatenates `linkerOpts.ios` of every .def in the published modules plus KiteFFmpeg's, and a test that the README block equals it. Add a Gradle static-framework consumer under verification/ linked by xcodebuild with only the README flags.

**How to check it yourself:** Diff README.md:113 against kiteplayer-libass/native/libass.def:21 and KiteFFmpeg kiteffmpeg/interop/ffmpeg.def:30; the union is what a static framework consumer needs. For proof, download ass-chain-ios-arm64.zip from the pinned KiteFFmpeg release and run `nm -u lib/libass.a lib/libharfbuzz.a | grep -E '_iconv|_CTFont|__ZNSt|_CG'` to see the undefined symbols, or link a scratch static framework with only the README flags and read the undefined-symbol errors.

**Verifier's note:** README.md:113 reads exactly `-ObjC -lz -framework CoreFoundation -framework CoreMedia -framework CoreVideo -framework VideoToolbox -framework AudioToolbox`, and README.md:109-110 presents it as what a static framework needs. That is KiteFFmpeg's list: /home/user/KiteFFmpeg/kiteffmpeg/interop/ffmpeg.def:30 `linkerOpts.ios = -lz -framework CoreFoundation -framework CoreMedia -framework CoreVideo -framework VideoToolbox -framework AudioToolbox` (plus -ObjC). kiteplayer-libass/native/libass.def:21 `linkerOpts.ios = -lz -liconv -lc++ -framework CoreText -framework CoreFoundation -framework CoreGraphics`, with the comment at lines 17-19 explaining Apple ships `its C++ runtime as libc++`. KiteFFmpeg's own chain test agrees on what the archives need: /home/user/KiteFFmpeg/scripts/test-ass-chain.sh:27 `Darwin) system=(-lc++ -liconv -framework CoreText -framework CoreFoundation -framework CoreGraphics)`. kiteplayer/module.yaml:19 `//kiteplayer-libass: exported`, so every consumer of `kiteplayer` links libkiteass.a. kiteplayer-rt/native/kitert.def:35 adds `-framework AudioToolbox`, already in the README list. The iOS sample's pbxproj line 138 runs `"${KOTLIN_CLI_WRAPPER_PATH}" tool xcode-integration` and has no OTHER_LDFLAGS, so it never exercises the hand-written list. Missing from the README for a static framework: -liconv, -lc++, -framework CoreText, -framework CoreGraphics. No other README or docs line mentions liconv, lc++ or CoreText for iOS setup (grep over README.md, docs/*.md, CHANGELOG.md).

### F-134 Stale KDoc sentences in PlayerConfig and PlaybackError misdescribe the surface

**Severity:** low · **Kind:** Documentation · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** docs/kdoc · **Lane:** public-api-and-docs · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high · **Related open issue:** 676

**Where:**

- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/PlayerConfig.kt:398-401`
- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/PlayerConfig.kt:21-22`
- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/PlaybackError.kt:117-131`
- `kiteplayer-ffmpeg/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/ffmpeg/KiteFFmpegSource.kt:118-125`
- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/internal/ItemClip.kt:51-55`
- `kiteplayer/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/KitePlayers.kt:43`

**Evidence:** PlayerConfig.kt 398-399 (volumeCeiling): "Last in the list on purpose: inserting it earlier would move `downmix`'s position and break every caller that passed it positionally." followed at 402-444 by equalizer, replayGain, replayGainPreampDb, replayGainFallbackDb, resampler, upmix and matchOutputChannels. PlayerConfig.kt 21-22: "The members nothing reads are marked one by one below, each with a pointer to where they are decided." (`grep -n "nothing reads"` finds only this sentence). PlaybackError.kt 117: "Three cases today." for ConfigurationInvalid, while MediaItem.kt 143-145 (audioFilter on the web), 262-263 (a clip starting past the end) and KitePlayers.kt 161-162 (no default stack) add further cases.

**Claim (as corrected by the verifier):** Three KDoc sentences are stale: volumeCeiling is described as last in AudioConfig while seven fields follow it; PlayerConfig promises per-member markers of what the core does not read and only one such note exists (line 170); PlaybackError.ConfigurationInvalid says "Three cases today" while two more exist (audioFilter without filter graphs, a clip starting past the end). The no-default-stack throw in KitePlayers.kt is the documented missing-backend case, not a new one.

**Finder's original claim:** Three sentences describe a state of the code that no longer holds. The volumeCeiling one is the riskiest: it records a positional-compatibility rule that later fields already broke, so a reader may trust an ordering guarantee that does not exist (see #676 for the general data-class problem; this adds a specific false claim).

**Scenario:** A reader of the API site takes the "last in the list" sentence as a promise about positional construction of AudioConfig, or searches PlayerConfig for the promised "nothing reads" markers.

**Impact:** Small credibility cost in otherwise careful KDoc.

**Suggested fix:** Delete or rewrite the three sentences: say AudioConfig fields are appended at the end and callers should use named arguments; drop the "marked one by one" clause; list the ConfigurationInvalid cases or say "among them".

**How to check it yourself:** Read PlayerConfig.kt 398-446 and count fields after volumeCeiling; grep -n 'ConfigurationInvalid(' across kiteplayer-core/src, kiteplayer/src and kiteplayer-ffmpeg/src and compare the sites (KiteFFmpegSource.kt 121, ItemClip.kt 52, FFmpegRuntimeCheck.kt 36, DemuxPolicyTranslation.kt 31, KitePlayer.kt 1908/1915, KitePlayers.kt 43) against the three cases named at PlaybackError.kt 117-131.

**Verifier's note:** PlayerConfig.kt 398-399 (volumeCeiling KDoc): "Last in the list on purpose: inserting it earlier would move `downmix`'s position and break every caller that passed it positionally." followed by `val volumeCeiling: Float = 1f,` at 401 and then equalizer (403), replayGain (414), replayGainPreampDb (416), replayGainFallbackDb (418), resampler (424), upmix (429), matchOutputChannels (446): seven fields after the one described as last. PlayerConfig.kt 21-22: "The members nothing reads are marked one by one below, each with a pointer to where they are decided." The only marker-like sentence is line 170 ("An explicit [ioResolver] does not read this field"), nothing else is marked. PlaybackError.kt 117 "Three cases today." then lists missing backend, runtime mismatch, option set twice; but ConfigurationInvalid is also thrown at kiteplayer-ffmpeg KiteFFmpegSource.kt 121 ("MediaItem.audioFilter needs FFmpeg filter graphs, and this build has none") and kiteplayer-core internal/ItemClip.kt 52 ("the item's clip starts at ..., and the media is only ... long"), both promised by MediaItem.kt 143-145 and 262-263. Two corrections: the KitePlayers.kt citation is wrong, that file is 95 lines and the throw is at line 43 (`?: throw PlaybackException(PlaybackError.ConfigurationInvalid(noDefaultStackDetail()))`), and that case is the documented first case (a missing backend), not a new one. The stale sentences are real; #676 is about binary breaks in general and does not cover these specific false sentences.

### F-135 Two KDoc blocks are orphaned, leaving setDialogueLevel and setVideoScale undocumented on the API site

**Severity:** low · **Kind:** Documentation · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** docs/kdoc · **Lane:** public-api-and-docs · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

**Where:**

- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/KitePlayer.kt:466-491`
- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/KitePlayer.kt:518-519`
- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/KitePlayer.kt:664-690`

**Evidence:** KitePlayer.kt 466-478: a KDoc block beginning "Raises or lowers the centre channel, where a film's dialogue lives, by [db] decibels" is immediately followed at 479-490 by a second KDoc block "Moves the pitch by [semitones]" and then 491 `public fun setPitch(semitones: Double)`. 518-519: `@Throws(...) public fun setDialogueLevel(db: Float)` has no KDoc above it. 664-675: a block "Sets how the picture occupies its surface: whole picture letterboxed ([VideoScale.Fit]" is followed at 676-684 by the redrawPicture block and 685 `public fun redrawPicture()`; 690 `public fun setVideoScale(mode: VideoScale)` has only @Throws above it.

**Claim:** Kotlin attaches only the last KDoc comment before a declaration; a KDoc block followed by another KDoc block is dropped by Dokka. So the dialogue-level and video-scale documentation, including their @throws ranges, does not appear on the published API reference, and both setters show as undocumented. Dokka runs with warnings as errors for unresolved links but does not flag dangling comments.

**Scenario:** A developer opens the KitePlayer page on yuroyami.github.io looking for the dialogue level's range or what the scale modes mean and finds no text; IDE quick documentation on setDialogueLevel is empty.

**Impact:** Two public setters have no documentation where developers look, while the text exists in the source.

**Suggested fix:** Move the block at 466-478 to sit directly above setDialogueLevel (518) and the block at 664-675 directly above setVideoScale (690). Consider a repo check that fails on `*/` followed by `/**` with only whitespace between.

**How to check it yourself:** Run ./kotlin do dokka -m kiteplayer-core and open the KitePlayer page: setDialogueLevel and setVideoScale have no description. Or `awk` for consecutive KDoc blocks in KitePlayer.kt.

**Verifier's note:** KitePlayer.kt 466-478 is a KDoc block starting "Raises or lowers the centre channel, where a film's dialogue lives, by [db] decibels" ending with "@throws IllegalArgumentException when [db] is not finite or is more than [DIALOGUE_LEVEL_MAX_DB] either way." and line 479 immediately opens a second `/**` block ("Moves the pitch by [semitones]") that ends at 490 before `public fun setPitch` at 491. Lines 518-519 are `@Throws(IllegalStateException::class, IllegalArgumentException::class)` then `public fun setDialogueLevel(db: Float)` with only `setSkipSilence`'s body above them, no comment. Likewise 664-671 ("Sets how the picture occupies its surface") is followed at 672 by `/**` "Draws the picture on screen again (#438)" ending at 684 before `public fun redrawPicture()` at 685, and 689-690 `@Throws(...) public fun setVideoScale(mode: VideoScale)` has no KDoc. Kotlin attaches only the doc comment immediately preceding a declaration, so both first blocks are orphaned and Dokka/IDE show setDialogueLevel and setVideoScale undocumented. Line numbers are exact.

### F-136 Licensing prose contradicts the tree: NOTICE names folders that do not exist, LICENSE describes a GPL flavour KiteFFmpeg says it never publishes, and kiteplayer-output's POM omits a bundled licence

**Severity:** low · **Kind:** Documentation · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** docs/licensing · **Lane:** build-distribution-tests-ci · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

**Where:**

- `NOTICE:33-35`
- `NOTICE:62-64`
- `NOTICE:87-89`
- `LICENSE:17-20`
- `NOTICE:17-21`
- `kiteplayer-output/module.yaml:37-40`

**Evidence:** NOTICE:34-35: `kiteplayer-libass/src/jvmMain/resources/META-INF/licenses/kiteplayer-libass/`; NOTICE:63-64: `kiteplayer-audioviz/src/jvmMain/resources/META-INF/licenses/kiteplayer-audioviz/`; NOTICE:88-89: `kiteplayer-output/src/androidMain/resources/META-INF/licenses/kiteplayer-output/`. `find . -type d -name licenses` finds only `kiteplayer-libass/resources@jvm/META-INF/licenses`, `kiteplayer-audioviz/resources@jvm/...`, `kiteplayer-output/resources@android/...` and their siblings; no `src/jvmMain` exists anywhere. LICENSE:17-20: `GPL when --enable-gpl is set, effectively GPL-3.0 for KiteFFmpeg's GPL build flavour, which also sets --enable-version3`; KiteFFmpeg NOTICE:72-73: `As of 0.1.0 this project builds and publishes NO GPL flavour.` NOTICE:17-21 says the KiteFFmpeg artifacts `embed exactly two third-party components ... nothing else is linked`, while KiteFFmpeg NOTICE:101-102 also lists `compiler-rt ... bundled in the androidNativeArm64 klib`. kiteplayer-output/module.yaml has `pom:` with name and description only and no `licenses:`, while NOTICE:80-87 says its Android and Apple artifacts carry Anime4K weights under MIT; kiteplayer-audioviz and kiteplayer-subtitles do declare their bundled licences.

**Claim:** The README tells native-app authors to take the licence texts `from the sources listed in NOTICE`, and the three paths NOTICE lists are Gradle-layout paths that this toolchain never had. LICENSE's GPL sentence describes a flavour the sibling explicitly does not publish. The NOTICE sentence about `exactly two` components is contradicted by the sibling's own component list. The output module's POM declares Apache only although its AAR ships MIT-licensed network weights. None of this changes what ships, but these are the files a licence reviewer reads first.

**Scenario:** A native iOS or macOS app author follows NOTICE to collect the FriBidi and libass texts, finds no such folder, and either skips the notice or files an issue. A compliance scan of the kiteplayer-output POM reports only Apache-2.0 for an artifact that carries MIT material.

**Impact:** Avoidable licence-compliance friction and three statements that a stranger can prove false in one `ls`.

**Suggested fix:** Replace the three NOTICE paths with `resources@jvm/META-INF/licenses/...` and `resources@android/...`; delete or rewrite the GPL sentence in LICENSE to match KiteFFmpeg's NOTICE; change `exactly two` to the sibling's component list or point at it only; add `licenses:` with the Anime4K MIT entry to kiteplayer-output/module.yaml as audioviz does. A one-line test in build-support could assert every path named in NOTICE exists.

**How to check it yourself:** `ls kiteplayer-libass/src/jvmMain kiteplayer-audioviz/src/jvmMain kiteplayer-output/src/androidMain` (all missing); `find . -type d -name licenses -not -path '*/build/*'`; `grep -n 'GPL' LICENSE NOTICE ../KiteFFmpeg/NOTICE`; `grep -n -A8 'pom:' kiteplayer-output/module.yaml kiteplayer-audioviz/module.yaml`.

**Verifier's note:** Every quoted line exists. NOTICE:35 `kiteplayer-libass/src/jvmMain/resources/META-INF/licenses/kiteplayer-libass/`, NOTICE:64 `kiteplayer-audioviz/src/jvmMain/resources/...`, NOTICE:89 `kiteplayer-output/src/androidMain/resources/...`. `find . -type d -name licenses` (excluding build/) finds only `resources@jvm` and `resources@android` folders under kiteplayer-output, kiteplayer-audioviz, kiteplayer-subtitles and kiteplayer-libass; `ls kiteplayer-libass/src/jvmMain` is `No such file or directory`, same for the other two. README.md:513 sends native-app authors to `the sources listed in [NOTICE](NOTICE)`. LICENSE:18-20: `GPL when --enable-gpl is set, effectively GPL-3.0 for KiteFFmpeg's GPL build flavour, which also sets --enable-version3`, while KiteFFmpeg NOTICE:72 says `As of 0.1.0 this project builds and publishes NO GPL flavour` and KitePlayer's own NOTICE:21 says `KiteFFmpeg publishes no GPL flavour`. NOTICE:17-21 says the artifacts `embed exactly two third-party components` and `nothing else is linked`; KiteFFmpeg NOTICE:101-102 lists `compiler-rt ... bundled in the androidNativeArm64 klib`. kiteplayer-output/module.yaml:36-39 has `pom: name: ... description: ...` and no `licenses:`; library.module-template.yaml:20-22 supplies only `Apache License 2.0`; kiteplayer-audioviz/module.yaml:40-43, kiteplayer-subtitles/module.yaml:45-47 and kiteplayer-libass/module.yaml:48-53 each add their bundled licences. Anime4kNetworks.kt sits in `kiteplayer-output/src@androidAndApple/`, so the Android AAR and Apple klibs do carry the MIT weights. Nothing in the build checks NOTICE paths or POM licence lists against bundled material (PublicationReadiness.kt:126-133 only requires one nonblank licence).
