### F-137 The Compose canvas path tone maps HDR on every platform, so a 360 degree HDR video cannot be both spherical and HDR, and the README's HDR cells do not say so.

**Severity:** low · **Kind:** Documentation · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** docs/platform-matrix · **Lane:** design-capabilities-crossmatch · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

**Where:**

- `README.md:49-50`
- `README.md:545-548`
- `kiteplayer-compose-video/src@threaded/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/compose/KiteVideoRenderer.kt:148-317`
- `kiteplayer-output/src@apple/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/output/MetalVideoRenderer.kt:643-651`

**Evidence:** README.md:49 `| **HDR on an HDR screen** | In \`KitePlayerView\` | ✓ | ✓ | | |`. README.md:545-547: "you can only look around in a 360 degree video where `KiteVideo` draws it. The native views ... show the whole frame flat, so pass `path = KiteRenderPath.ComposeCanvas` there." Override grep: KiteVideoRenderer overrides setAdjustments, setFlashGuard, setTransform, projects, setRenderQuality, videoDecoderFactories, supportedHardwareSurfaces, and neither showsHdr nor setHdrPolicy; only MetalVideoRenderer (:643, :651) and AndroidSurfaceVideoRenderer (:388, :413) do.

**Claim:** From code, HDR is shown as HDR by exactly two renderers: the Metal renderer behind KitePlayerUIView and the AppKit Metal layer, and the Android surface renderer on its codec path. KiteVideoRenderer, which every KiteRenderPath.ComposeCanvas and every 360 degree view uses, has no HDR path, so it tone maps. The README's iOS and macOS HDR ticks are true for the default native path but become false the moment the same README tells the reader to switch to ComposeCanvas for 360 degree video or for Compose clipping and alpha.

**Scenario:** An iOS app shows a 360 degree HDR clip (common on 360 cameras) and follows README.md:547 to pass ComposeCanvas; the picture tone maps to SDR and PlaybackWarning.HdrToneMapped fires, which the app's author reads as a bug because the table said iOS shows HDR.

**Impact:** Misleading platform table for a headline feature; integrators cannot plan which path to use.

**Suggested fix:** Add a footnote to the HDR row: "through the native view path; the Compose canvas path and the 360 degree view tone map everywhere", and the same sentence in docs/spherical-video.md.

**How to check it yourself:** grep -rn 'showsHdr\|setHdrPolicy' kiteplayer-compose-video/src* (no hits) and read VideoRenderer.kt:116-121 and :210-217 for what the defaults mean. Then read README.md:48 against :544-547 and KiteRenderPath.kt:5-19. On a device: play an HDR clip with KitePlayerVideo(path = KiteRenderPath.ComposeCanvas) on an iPhone and read PlayerSnapshot.videoDynamicRange and the HdrToneMapped warning.

**Verifier's note:** Verified. README.md:48 `| **HDR on an HDR screen** | In \`KitePlayerView\` | ✓ | ✓ | | |` qualifies only the Android cell. README.md:544-547 tells the reader that for 360 degree video the native views "show the whole frame flat, so pass `path = KiteRenderPath.ComposeCanvas` there", and docs/spherical-video.md:141-142 repeats it in code. grep showsHdr, setHdrPolicy and HdrShown over kiteplayer-compose-video/src*: no hits, so KiteVideoRenderer keeps VideoRenderer.kt:217 `public val showsHdr: Boolean get() = false` and :121 `setHdrPolicy(...) {}`, whose KDoc reads "The default ignores it, for a renderer that always tone maps." KiteVideoRenderer.kt:111-112 and :376-380 confirm the path tone maps and emits RendererEvent.ToneMapEngaged, with kiteCodecToneMaps on ios (ImageBitmaps.ios.kt:91), jvm (:50) and android (:50) all delegating to SoftwareConverter.toneMapsHdr. The only hardware-backed Compose path, KiteVideoHardwareRenderer, has an implementation on Android alone (ImageBitmaps.android.kt:90-93), and it too overrides neither HDR member. The renderers that override showsHdr are MetalVideoRenderer (MetalVideoRenderer.kt:643-648) and AndroidSurfaceVideoRenderer (:410-412), as the finding says. KiteRenderPath's KDoc (KiteRenderPath.kt:5-19) names input and frame-rate costs of ComposeCanvas but not HDR, and no doc under docs/ ties HDR to a renderer. So the iOS and macOS ticks are true for the default path and silently false on the path the same README sends a 360 degree viewer to. Docs finding, low, as filed.

KiteFFmpeg BuildFFmpegTask.kt 387: `"--enable-protocol=file,fd,pipe,data,http,tcp,udp,rtp,rtmp"`, comment at 377 "udp, rtp and rtmp joined on 2026-10-03 (#124)". The engine itself treats the wider set as live: kiteplayer-ffmpeg FallbackSchemes.kt 20 `internal val realTimeSchemes: Set<String> = setOf("udp", "rtp", "rtsp", "rtmp")` and ItemSources.kt 315-316 give rtmp `rw_timeout` and udp/rtsp `timeout`. ### F-139 README and player-api.md promise that nothing is silently ignored, which the fire-and-forget setters' own KDoc contradicts

**Severity:** low · **Kind:** Documentation · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** docs/readme · **Lane:** public-api-and-docs · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

**Where:**

- `README.md:296-298`
- `docs/player-api.md:39-40`
- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/KitePlayer.kt:219-221`
- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/KitePlayer.kt:737-738`
- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/DemuxPolicy.kt:109-111`

**Evidence:** README 296-298: "When the player cannot do what a call asks, the call fails with a typed error. It is never silently ignored." player-api.md 39-40: "The player refuses anything it cannot do with a typed error, instead of accepting the call and ignoring it." KitePlayer.kt 219-221 (requestSeek): "Nothing is thrown when the source cannot seek: a call that does not wait has nobody to throw to, so it is ignored." KitePlayer.kt 737-738 (setRenderQuality): "A renderer honours what it can and ignores the rest, so this never fails and never blocks." DemuxPolicy.kt 109-111: "An index that the master playlist does not have is ignored, and the choice is made as for null." setAbLoop KDoc: a refused arm "is published as a [PlaybackWarning.CommandRefused] on [events]" rather than thrown.

**Claim:** The blanket sentence is true for suspending calls and for argument validation, and false for the fire-and-forget members, whose refusals arrive as warnings or are dropped by design. The README states a stronger contract than the API keeps.

**Scenario:** A developer relies on the README, calls requestSeek on a live stream or setRenderQuality(Standard) on the Android view path, sees no exception, and assumes the request took effect.

**Impact:** Misleading top-level promise; low because the per-member KDoc is accurate.

**Suggested fix:** Qualify both sentences: suspending calls throw a typed error; setters that return at once report a refusal as PlaybackWarning.CommandRefused on events (or, for a renderer that cannot honour a value, do nothing), and name requestSeek as the deliberate exception.

**How to check it yourself:** Read README.md 296-298 and docs/player-api.md 39-40 against KitePlayer.kt 220-221, 737-738, 648-649 and DemuxPolicy.kt 109-111; then PlaybackCore.kt 3011-3020, where a `SeekLater` on an unseekable source is dropped with `clearSeekMaskUnlessPending()` and no warning.

**Verifier's note:** README.md 296-298: "When the player cannot do what a call asks, the call fails with a typed error. It is never silently ignored." docs/player-api.md 39-40: "The player refuses anything it cannot do with a typed error, instead of accepting the call and ignoring it." KitePlayer.kt 220-221 (requestSeek): "Nothing is thrown when the source cannot seek: a call that does not wait has nobody to throw to, so it is ignored." I traced the engine side: PlaybackCore.kt 3011-3020 handles `CoreCommand.SeekLater` with `else if (session?.source?.seekable == true || pendingVideoRecovery != null) { queueSeek(command.request, null) } else { // Dropped: ... clearSeekMaskUnlessPending() }`, with no warning published, so the drop is silent in the strict sense. KitePlayer.kt 737-738 (setRenderQuality): "A renderer honours what it can and ignores the rest, so this never fails and never blocks." DemuxPolicy.kt 109-111: "An index that the master playlist does not have is ignored, and the choice is made as for null." setAbLoop KDoc 648-649 routes a refusal to `PlaybackWarning.CommandRefused` rather than an exception. The blanket README sentence overstates the contract for the fire-and-forget members. Docs judgement, evidence holds.

### F-140 README's worker download size of 0.7 MB predates the Ktor growth the CHANGELOG records

**Severity:** low · **Kind:** Documentation · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** docs/readme · **Lane:** public-api-and-docs · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** low

**Where:**

- `README.md:504-505`
- `scripts/check-web-size.sh:68-78`
- `scripts/check-web-size.sh:89-92`
- `CHANGELOG.md:130-132`

**Evidence:** README 504-505: "On the web, the page downloads about 1.5 MB for the codec module and 0.7 MB for the worker player, with gzip." check-web-size.sh 89-92: `# 1.47 MiB.` `BUDGET_BYTES=1541407` `# 0.86 MiB.` `WORKER_BUDGET_BYTES=901775`, and the file's header says a budget is raised only in the commit that moved the size. CHANGELOG [Unreleased]: "The worker binary in `kiteplayer-wasm-js-<version>-web.zip` is 119,963 bytes larger after gzip. It now links `kiteplayer-network` and Ktor".

**Claim (as corrected by the verifier):** README.md:504-505 says the worker player downloads about 0.7 MB gzipped. The size script's own record of the last measurement is 891,876 bytes (0.85 MiB, about 0.9 MB), with a budget of 901,775 bytes, because the worker now links kiteplayer-network and Ktor (+119,963 bytes) and grew again in the issue sweep (+14,408). The README understates the worker by about 170 KB; the codec figure of 1.5 MB matches its 1,538,723 bytes.

**Finder's original claim:** The worker budget is 902 KB gzipped and budgets track the measured size closely; after the recorded 120 KB growth the worker is most likely around 0.8 to 0.9 MB, not 0.7 MB. The codec figure matches its budget; the worker figure appears stale.

**Scenario:** An embedder sizing a page's first load trusts the README figure and under-budgets by 100 to 200 KB.

**Impact:** Minor misstatement of download cost.

**Suggested fix:** Run scripts/check-web-size.sh, read the worker row, and put the measured figure in the README (or say "under 0.9 MB").

**How to check it yourself:** Without a build: read the last two paragraphs of the header of scripts/check-web-size.sh (the 877,468 and 891,876 byte figures) and the `WORKER_BUDGET_BYTES=901775` line, and compare with README.md line 504. With a build: ./scripts/check-web-size.sh runs scripts/web-zips.sh worker and prints the gzipped size of each worker file and their sum; the CI run's `web-size` artifact (ci.yml line 1228) holds the same table for the last push.

**Verifier's note:** README.md:504-505 reads "On the web, the page downloads about 1.5 MB for the codec module and 0.7 MB for the worker player, with gzip." scripts/check-web-size.sh records its own measurements in the header: lines 68-71 "The worker measured 757,505 bytes without kiteplayer-network and 877,468 bytes with it, 119,963 more." and lines 74-78 "The worker grew from the 877,468 bytes measured at the last change to 891,876, 14,408 more and 587 over the budget before. The codec module kept its 1,538,723 bytes." with line 92 `WORKER_BUDGET_BYTES=901775` under the comment `# 0.86 MiB.` (the finding cited lines 89-92; the two budget lines are at 89-92 in the file as it stands, so no drift). 891,876 bytes gzipped is 0.85 MiB, about 0.9 MB in decimal units, against the README's 0.7 MB; the codec figure is right (1,538,723 bytes is 1.5 MB). Git history sharpens it: the README line and the CHANGELOG line "The worker binary ... is 119,963 bytes larger after gzip" (CHANGELOG.md:130) landed in the same commit, 0cf3185 on 2026-11-01 00:51, and the budget raise to 0.86 MiB (a7ece18) followed at 03:22 the same day, so the 0.7 MB was never the measured figure of the shipped worker; it was the pre-Ktor size (757,548 bytes, itself 0.76 MB) rounded down. No other document gives a worker size (grep of README.md and docs/ finds only this line). The CLAUDE.md note that the worker "costs 119,963 bytes after gzip" agrees with the script. Nothing guards the README against the script's ratchet, so the finding stands.

### F-040 External subtitle KDoc says SubRip and WebVTT while the code accepts TTML, ASS, LRC and a dozen FFmpeg formats

**Severity:** medium · **Kind:** Documentation · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** docs/subtitles · **Lane:** public-api-and-docs · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/MediaItem.kt:54-55`

MediaItem.kt 54-55: "Local SubRip and WebVTT files become selectable synthetic subtitle tracks". MediaItem.kt 538: "SubRip, WebVTT and ASS files load at open". docs/subtitles.md 9: "SubRip, WebVTT and SubStation Alpha, from the container or from an external file." KiteFFmpegMediaBackend.kt 50-52 KDoc: "External subtitle files, ASS, TTML and LRC lyrics included: the pure parsers this module ships, and FFmpeg's own readers for every other format (#492)"; 58-67 routes TtmlParser, AssParser, WebVttParser, LrcParser, SubRipParser. SubtitleFiles.kt 20-22: "SAMI, MicroDVD, SubViewer and SBV, MPL2, JACOsub, VPlayer, PJS, RealText, Spruce STL, Scenarist SCC, and the image tracks of VobSub and Blu-ray `.sup` files."

**Claim (as corrected by the verifier):** The KDoc of addExternalSubtitle, MediaItem.externalSubtitles and SubtitleSource, and the Formats bullet of docs/subtitles.md, name two or three external file formats and disagree with each other, while the one shared parse path accepts TTML, ASS, LRC and, through SubtitleFiles, eleven more FFmpeg text formats plus VobSub and PGS image files; the README's format list is wider and closer to the truth, so the fix is to make the three KDoc sentences and the guide match it.

**Finder's original claim:** Three public KDoc sentences and the subtitles guide understate the external-file contract to two or three formats, and they disagree with each other (two say SRT+VTT, one says SRT+VTT+ASS). The code accepts TTML, ASS, LRC and, through FFmpeg, eleven more text formats plus VobSub and PGS image files, including for addExternalSubtitle during playback (same parseExternalSubtitle path in PlaybackCore 676-760).

**Scenario:** A developer reading the API reference decides whether to let users pick .idx/.sub or .sup files, or a .ttml file, and concludes the player cannot load them; or a user files a bug when a .sami file loads "although the docs say it cannot".

**Impact:** A shipping capability is invisible from the public surface, and the three sentences contradict one another.

**Suggested fix:** Rewrite the three KDoc sentences and the docs/subtitles.md Formats bullet to name the real set (text: SubRip, WebVTT, ASS/SSA, TTML, LRC, and via FFmpeg SAMI, MicroDVD, SubViewer, SBV, MPL2, JACOsub, VPlayer, PJS, RealText, STL, SCC; image: VobSub .idx/.sub, Blu-ray .sup), and say which need the FFmpeg backend.

**How to check it yourself:** Read KiteFFmpegMediaBackend.kt 50-69 and SubtitleFiles.kt 19-27, then call addExternalSubtitle(SubtitleSource("movie.sup")) on the JVM: a track is added.

**Verifier's note:** All quoted sentences exist: KitePlayer.kt 981 'SubRip and WebVTT, the same text path the open-time route reads.' in addExternalSubtitle's KDoc; MediaItem.kt 54-55 'Local SubRip and WebVTT files become selectable synthetic subtitle tracks'; MediaItem.kt 538 'SubRip, WebVTT and ASS files load at open'; docs/subtitles.md 9 'SubRip, WebVTT and SubStation Alpha, from the container or from an external file. External files load in the middle of playback.' The code is wider: KiteFFmpegMediaBackend.kt 50-69 routes TtmlParser, AssParser, WebVttParser, LrcParser and SubRipParser, and its line 76 hands anything else to `SubtitleFiles.read(bytes, text, uri)`, whose KDoc (SubtitleFiles.kt 19-22) names SAMI, MicroDVD, SubViewer, SBV, MPL2, JACOsub, VPlayer, PJS, RealText, Spruce STL, Scenarist SCC, VobSub and Blu-ray .sup. The same path serves both routes: PlaybackCore.kt 676 `parseExternalSubtitle` calls `backend.subtitleFileParser()` and at 739-744 'A format the text readers do not know is the parser's other readers' to read (#492)' via `parser.parseOther`, and the addExternalSubtitle command at 851 and the replace path at 971 call that same `parseExternalSubtitle`. The three public sentences disagree with each other and all understate the contract. One softening: README 338-344 lists the format matrix more fully (ASS/SSA, SubRip, WebVTT, TTML, image subtitles, closed captions, synced lyrics) and docs/subtitles.md 37 mentions .lrc files, so a reader of the README alone is not misled; the API reference and the subtitles guide's own Formats bullet are.

### F-141 The libass web files are GitHub release assets, not an attachment of the Maven artifact, and the default ./kiteass.mjs resolves against the Kotlin glue module rather than the page, contrary to the KDoc and CLAUDE.md

**Severity:** low · **Kind:** Documentation · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** docs/web-delivery · **Lane:** web-worker-wasm-libass · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

**Where:**

- `kiteplayer-libass/src@wasmJs/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/libass/KiteLibassWeb.kt:13-26`
- `kiteplayer-libass/src@wasmJs/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/libass/KiteLibassWeb.kt:54`
- `kiteplayer-libass/src@wasmJs/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/libass/KiteLibassWeb.kt:137-140`
- `kiteplayer-libass/src@wasmJs/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/libass/LibassEngine.wasmJs.kt:204`
- `CLAUDE.md:653-654`
- `scripts/web-zips.sh:8-9`
- `README.md:148-150`
- `kiteplayer/src@wasmJs/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/KitePlayerWorker.kt:636-640`
- `kiteplayer/src@wasmJs/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/KitePlayerWorker.kt:698-705`

**Evidence:** KiteLibassWeb.kt:311-313 "The two files come as the `web` zip attached to this module's wasmJs artifact; unpack them beside the page." CLAUDE.md:653-654 "delivered as the `web` zip on the wasmJs publication". web-zips.sh:8-9 "A Kotlin Toolchain publication carries no extra files, so the zips go to the GitHub release page, not Maven Central." README.md:149-150 "KitePlayer's two zips are assets of the KitePlayer release on GitHub". KiteLibassWeb.kt:433 `import(/* webpackIgnore: true */ url)` runs inside the generated glue module, so a relative URL resolves against that module's location; KitePlayerWorker.kt:640 says the same: "the first ASS track then looks beside the worker binary."

**Claim (as corrected by the verifier):** KiteLibassWeb's KDoc (lines 17-19) and CLAUDE.md:653-654 say the kiteass.mjs/kiteass.wasm zip is attached to the wasmJs Maven publication, while scripts/web-zips.sh, publish.yml and the README say the zips are GitHub release assets only. The KDoc also says to unpack the files `beside the page` and that a page then `needs no code here`, but the default `./kiteass.mjs` is resolved by a dynamic import emitted into the Kotlin/Wasm glue module, so it is read beside that glue, not beside index.html; the worker facade's default libassUrl is page-relative because it passes through pageAddress, so the mismatch affects the page's own KitePlayer and a worker started with libassUrl = null (which the worker KDoc describes correctly).

**Finder's original claim:** Two statements in the code's own documentation are untrue: where the module comes from (release page, not the artifact) and where the default address points (beside the Kotlin .mjs glue, not beside index.html). A page that keeps its scripts in a subfolder follows the KDoc, puts kiteass.mjs beside index.html, and the first ASS track silently falls back to the built-in styling after ten seconds.

**Scenario:** An embedder reads the KiteLibassWeb KDoc, looks for a `web` classifier on Maven Central, finds none, and after finding the GitHub asset unpacks it beside index.html while the page's module bundle sits in /assets/; ASS tracks draw with the built-in styling with a TypesetterUnavailable warning after the deadline.

**Impact:** Setup failures on the one platform where libass needs a hosting step.

**Suggested fix:** Rewrite the KiteLibassWeb KDoc and CLAUDE.md to say the files are GitHub release assets, and that DEFAULT_URL resolves against the location of the Kotlin module that imports it (`new URL('./kiteass.mjs', import.meta.url)` semantics); recommend `KiteLibassWeb.load(absoluteUrl)` or the worker's libassUrl for pages that split folders.

**How to check it yourself:** Compare KiteLibassWeb.kt:17-19 and CLAUDE.md:653-654 with scripts/web-zips.sh:8-9, publish.yml:24-27 and README.md:148-150. For the address: serve a page whose compiled Kotlin glue .mjs lives in /js/ and keep kiteass.mjs beside index.html; open an ASS file in the page's own KitePlayer (not the worker facade with its default) and watch the Network panel request /js/kiteass.mjs and the track fall back with TypesetterUnavailable after ten seconds.

**Verifier's note:** The cited line numbers are wrong (KiteLibassWeb.kt is 146 lines) but the text exists. KiteLibassWeb.kt:17-19: `The two files come as the \`web\` zip attached to this module's wasmJs artifact; unpack them beside the page. The first ASS track a player meets starts loading [DEFAULT_URL] on its own, so a page that serves the two files needs no code here.` CLAUDE.md:653-654: `delivered as the \`web\` zip on the wasmJs publication`. Against that, scripts/web-zips.sh:8-9: `A Kotlin Toolchain publication carries no extra files, so the zips go to the GitHub release page, not Maven Central.`, publish.yml:24-27 says the same and README.md:148-150 says `KitePlayer's two zips are assets of the KitePlayer release on GitHub`. No classifier or zip attachment exists in library.module-template.yaml or the module yaml files. So the provenance half is a plain contradiction in the KDoc and CLAUDE.md. On the address half: the default load is `KiteLibassWeb.loadInBackground()` (LibassEngine.wasmJs.kt:204) with `DEFAULT_URL = "./kiteass.mjs"` (KiteLibassWeb.kt:54), executed by `@JsFun("(url) => import(/* webpackIgnore: true */ url).then(m => m.default())")` at :139; a @JsFun body is emitted into the Kotlin/Wasm glue module, so a relative dynamic import resolves against that module's URL, not document.baseURI, and the worker KDoc at KitePlayerWorker.kt:640 confirms the same reading: `Null loads nothing now, and the first ASS track then looks beside the worker binary.` One narrowing: the worker facade's default parameter `libassUrl: String? = "./kiteass.mjs"` (:650) is passed through `pageAddress` (:705 `libassUrl = libassUrl?.let(::pageAddress)`), so with the default the worker path IS page-relative; the glue-relative resolution bites the page's own KitePlayer and a worker started with libassUrl = null. The KDoc's `beside the page` is only true when the Kotlin glue is served beside index.html.

### F-148 HwdecStatus.HardwareWithDownload is declared statically for every VideoToolbox and Direct3D route, whether or not the renderer actually downloads

**Severity:** low · **Kind:** Documentation · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** ffmpeg-backend/hwdec · **Lane:** ffmpeg-backend · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** medium

**Where:**

- `kiteplayer-ffmpeg/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/ffmpeg/KiteFFmpegSource.kt:1144-1152`
- `kiteplayer-ffmpeg/src@native/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/ffmpeg/MetalFrameAccess.kt:39-46`
- `kiteplayer-output/src@apple/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/output/MetalVideoRenderer.kt:477`
- `kiteplayer-view-bindings/src@ios/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/mobile/MobilePlayerViewRenderer.ios.kt:31`

**Evidence:** KiteFFmpegSource.kt:1144-1152 `// HardwareWithDownload is the honest status for BOTH shapes: mediacodec downloads inside FFmpeg's wrapper, and every current renderer reads a VideoToolbox frame through the download twin. This changes when the Metal renderer makes zero-copy real. hardware = if (route == null) { HwdecStatus.Software } else { HwdecStatus.HardwareWithDownload(route.kind) }`. MetalFrameAccess.kt:117-119 `/** The CVPixelBuffer of a VideoToolbox frame, or null when the frame is not that kind. */ public fun KiteFFmpegVideoFrame.corePixelBufferOrNull(): COpaquePointer? = if (hardwareSurface == HwSurfaceKind.CoreVideoPixelBuffer) frame.hardwareSurface else null`, and its KDoc :121-124 "downloading to feed a GPU that could wrap the surface directly would be the exact copy this path exists to avoid".

**Claim (as corrected by the verifier):** HwdecStatus.HardwareWithDownload is declared at decoder open for every hardware route, but the native Apple Metal and sample-buffer renderers draw the VideoToolbox CVPixelBuffer directly through corePixelBufferOrNull, so statistics report a download that does not happen there; the comment justifying the static status is out of date. JVM renderers do download, so the status is right for them.

**Finder's original claim:** The zero-copy door the comment says does not exist yet is exported from this module. Whether a download happens is decided per frame by the renderer (the lazy twin at :1832), but the status is fixed at decoder open, so statistics report 'hardware with download' for a Metal path that draws the pixel buffer directly, and the comment that justifies it is out of date.

**Scenario:** Apple native or macOS JVM with the Metal renderer; the stats line says the frames are downloaded.

**Impact:** Diagnostics claim a copy that may not happen; a performance investigation starts from a wrong fact.

**Suggested fix:** Report `Hardware(kind)` at open and let the frame record whether readableFrame() was ever called, which the engine's stats can sum; or at least update the comment to say the status is a conservative declaration.

**How to check it yourself:** On iOS or native macOS with the Metal renderer, play an H.264 file and read the hwdec status from the playback statistics; add a counter around KiteFFmpegVideoFrame.readableFrame()'s downloadFromHardware call and confirm it stays at zero while the status says HardwareWithDownload.

**Verifier's note:** KiteFFmpegSource.kt:1144-1152 is as quoted: the comment says 'every current renderer reads a VideoToolbox frame through the download twin. This changes when the Metal renderer makes zero-copy real' and the status is fixed at `HwdecStatus.HardwareWithDownload(route.kind)` for every route. Zero-copy is real today: kiteplayer-ffmpeg/src@native/.../MetalFrameAccess.kt:39-41 exports `corePixelBufferOrNull()`, and it is consumed by kiteplayer-view-bindings/src@ios/.../MobilePlayerViewRenderer.ios.kt:31, kiteplayer-compose-video/src@ios/.../ImageBitmaps.ios.kt:47 and kiteplayer-sample/src/Main.kt:152 as `MetalPicture.CorePixelBuffer`, which kiteplayer-output/src@apple MetalVideoRenderer.kt:477, MetalFrameComposer.kt:198/292/660 and SampleBufferVideoRenderer.kt:408 draw directly. PlayerState.kt:611 defines HardwareWithDownload as 'frames are downloaded to main memory before presentation', which is false on those paths. The only engine consumer of the distinction is PlaybackCore.kt:7294, which treats ZeroCopy and WithDownload alike, so the effect is on reported statistics only. Two corrections: the MetalFrameAccess line numbers are 39-46, not 117-124 (the file is 75 lines); and 'macOS JVM' is wrong, since corePixelBufferOrNull lives in src@native and no JVM renderer takes a CorePixelBuffer, so the JVM path really does download.

The flag is live: HlsOpening.kt:105 `val nested = io.location != null && nestedOpensSupported`. The wasmJs class KDoc at :12-27 still says 'A source that genuinely needs to await bytes is REFUSED here' and 'The general fix is a Worker ... at that point this class becomes the blocking bridge again', while blockingIn at :82-105 and its KDoc ('one that waits for the network inside a worker's synchronous request, opens a related address without suspending (#546)') describe the shipped Worker path. Fmp4RewriteTest.kt:226-227 shows the result: decode times 4000, 4001, 4002, 4040, 4080 for 40 ms frames, so the first two written durations are 1 tick and the third is 38.

**Claim (as corrected by the verifier):** After a joined rewrite the samples that decode ahead of the segment's first shown picture get decode times one tick apart, so their trun durations, and the packet and frame durations FFmpeg derives from them, are one tick (1 ms at a 1000 timescale) for the first few pictures of each joined segment, while presentation times stay exact. The player's cadence estimator and the Android display-rate request measure pts gaps and are unaffected; the carried duration is read only by `VideoPlayback.shownSlot`, `FrameQueue.bufferedUs` and the backward-step drop law, each by at most a frame or two at the join. The `Plan.joined` KDoc at Fmp4Rewrite.kt:35-39 should say that the first durations are not the frame's.

**Finder's original claim:** This is correct for presentation (I verified that composition times stay exact and cannot collide because the chain advances by one tick, not one frame), but FFmpeg's MP4 demuxer sets each packet's duration from the trun sample duration, so the first pictures after a Period join or variant switch arrive with a 1 ms duration. Anything downstream that trusts packet duration (frame-rate estimation on a fresh decoder, last-frame hold time, a `duration`-based cadence hint) sees a brief spike. The KDoc of Plan.joined (lines 35-39) does not say so.

**Scenario:** After a variant switch to a stream with more B-frames, a frame-rate estimator fed by packet durations reads 1000 fps for two packets.

**Impact:** None observed in this lane; worth a sentence in the Plan.joined KDoc so an engine-side consumer of packet duration knows to ignore it across a join.

**Suggested fix:** Document it on Plan.joined, or spread the delay over the first frames by advancing the floor by the source's own sample duration instead of one tick when that does not pass the sample's presentation time (it cannot in practice, since presentation is at least one frame after decode for a reordered stream).

**How to check it yourself:** Fmp4RewriteTest.kt:227 already shows the decode chain; add an assertion on `joined.map { it.duration }` expecting `listOf(1L, 1L, 38L, 40L, 40L)` to pin it. For FFmpeg's reading, write the bytes of `Fmp4Rewrite.rewrite(segment, Plan(init, init, 0, null, joined = true))` after the init to a file and run `ffprobe -show_packets -select_streams v` on it; the first two packets report `duration=1`.

**Verifier's note:** The byte-level mechanism is exactly as quoted. Fmp4Rewrite.kt:162 `for (i in kept.indices) decode[i] = placed(kept[i].decodeTime).coerceAtLeast((if (i == 0) after else decode[i - 1]) + 1)` and :184 `out.u32(decode[i + 1] - decode[i])` write the trun sample durations as the differences of the chained decode times, and Fmp4RewriteTest.kt:227 expects `listOf(4000L, 4001L, 4002L, 4040L, 4080L)` in a 1000 timescale, so the first two written durations are 1 ms and the third 38 ms, while :228 confirms every composition time is unchanged. The `Plan` KDoc at :35-39 speaks only of decode order and says nothing of durations. FFmpeg's MP4 reader takes a fragment packet's duration from the trun sample duration, and KiteFFmpegSource.kt:1264 `val duration = mapper.mapDuration(frame.durationMicros)` carries the decoder's duration into `VideoFrame.duration`, so the 1 ms does reach the engine. The downstream exposure is narrower than 'anything that trusts packet duration', because the player's own cadence paths were built not to: FrameDurationEstimator.kt:59-62 returns `snapped`, then `measured` (the pts gap, available across a join because an in-place variant switch keeps the generation), and only then `decoderReportedUs`, and the Android display-rate request SurfaceFrameRateRequest.kt:53-69 measures pts gaps (`val gapUs = ptsUs - last`), not durations, so the '1000 fps for two packets' scenario does not happen in this engine. What does read the carried duration: VideoPlayback.kt:453-454 `val carried = shown.duration?.micros; val durationUs = if (carried == null && lastNominalUs > 0) lastNominalUs else durations.estimate(null, carried)` (the slot of the last scheduled frame, masked once the estimator has snapped to the declared rate), FrameQueue.kt:74-78 `bufferedUs` (under-reads by one frame when the last queued frame is one of these), and VideoDropLaw.kt:81-82 `return pts + 2 * duration < discardBeforeUs` for a backward step landing on a joined boundary. Each is a one-or-two-frame effect at a Period join or variant switch, which fits the info/docs rating.

### F-166 docs/segment-cache.md says a partial read sends If-Range, but a record stored on max-age or Expires alone carries no validator and sends none.

**Severity:** low · **Kind:** Documentation · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** network/segment-store · **Lane:** network-adaptive-io · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

**Where:**

- `docs/segment-cache.md:99-101`
- `kiteplayer-network/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/network/SegmentFreshness.kt:279-283`
- `kiteplayer-network/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/network/KtorMediaIo.kt:578`
- `kiteplayer-network/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/network/KtorMediaIo.kt:659-676`

**Evidence:** Doc: `A read of a part that is not stored sends a range request with If-Range. When the server then answers with another file, the store removes the entry and that read fails.` (99-101). Code: `val tag = strongTag(facts.entityTag); val modified = facts.lastModified?.takeIf { httpDateSeconds(it) != null }; val lifetime = statedLifetime(...); if (tag == null && modified == null && lifetime == null) return null` (280-283), so a lifetime-only response is stored with both validators null. The gap read sends `(entityTag ?: lastModified?.takeIf { stored != null })?.let { header(HttpHeaders.IfRange, it) }` (566), nothing when both are null, and the only remaining guard is `if (size != null && total != size) { stored?.changed(); throw ... }` (587-594).

**Claim:** For a segment stored from a response with only Cache-Control max-age (or Expires), a later read of a part the store lacks is an unconditional range request, and a file replaced on the server with the same byte size within the lifetime is spliced onto the old bytes. The documented promise holds only for responses with a strong ETag or Last-Modified.

**Scenario:** A packager republishes a corrected segment of the same size (common for CMAF repackaging) under a CDN that sends only max-age; a player that stored half of it earlier reads the other half from the new file.

**Impact:** Rare silent corruption of one segment (a decode glitch), and a documentation claim that is not true as written.

**Suggested fix:** Either state in the doc that If-Range is sent only when the response had a strong ETag or Last-Modified, or refuse to serve partial lifetime-only entries (require holdsAll for a record with no validator, as is done for servers without ranges).

**How to check it yourself:** Run the KtorMediaIoSegmentStoreTest pattern of aChangeFoundInTheMiddleOfAFreshEntryFailsTheReadAndRemovesTheEntry with the segment served under `Cache-Control: max-age=3600` and no ETag or Last-Modified: the request log shows no If-Range and the read succeeds with mixed bytes.

**Verifier's note:** docs/segment-cache.md 99-101 reads `A read of a part that is not stored sends a range request with If-Range. When the server then answers with another file, the store removes the entry and that read fails.` while line 76 lists `a stated lifetime (max-age or Expires)` as enough to store a response. SegmentFreshness.kt 279-283 stores such a response with both validators null: `val tag = strongTag(facts.entityTag); val modified = facts.lastModified?.takeIf { httpDateSeconds(it) != null }; val lifetime = statedLifetime(...); if (tag == null && modified == null && lifetime == null) return null`. The gap read sends the header only when a validator exists, KtorMediaIo.kt 578 (not 566): `(entityTag ?: lastModified?.takeIf { stored != null })?.let { header(HttpHeaders.IfRange, it) }`. checkRangedAnswer's remaining guards are the total size, 659-663 `if (size != null && total != size) { stored?.changed(); throw ... }` (not 587-594), an entity tag comparison that needs `entityTag != null` (665-666), and a Last-Modified comparison that needs `lastModified != null` (672-676), so a same-size replacement under max-age alone is spliced onto the stored bytes. The documented promise therefore holds only for entries with a strong ETag or a Last-Modified, as the finding says.

### F-201 The samples sidestep Activity recreation with configChanges instead of showing the ViewModel ownership the README recommends

**Severity:** info · **Kind:** Documentation · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** samples/android · **Lane:** views-compose-ui-samples · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

**Where:**

- `kiteplayer-sample-android/src/AndroidManifest.xml:30-67`
- `kiteplayer-sample-android/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/sample/android/SampleController.kt:44-49`
- `kiteplayer-sample-android/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/sample/android/SampleController.kt:80-86`
- `kiteplayer-sample-android/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/sample/android/ComposeVideoActivity.kt:57-61`
- `kiteplayer-sample-android/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/sample/android/ComposeVideoActivity.kt:119-125`
- `README.md:216-218`
- `kiteplayer-compose/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/compose/RememberKitePlayer.kt:24-26`

**Evidence:** SampleController.kt 208-213: `fun openNormally(renderer: VideoRenderer? = null) { ... scope.launch { renderer?.let(player::attachRenderer); player.open(...) } }` on `Dispatchers.Default`. ComposeVideoActivity.kt 406-410: `LaunchedEffect(player, videoState) { withFrameNanos { }; controller.openNormally(videoState.renderer) }`. Every sample Activity has `configChanges` set in the manifest (AndroidManifest.xml 34, 52, 57), so the per-Activity player survives rotation only by opting out of recreation. README 216-218: `To keep playing through a rotation, keep the player in a ViewModel instead, and close it in onCleared.`

**Claim (as corrected by the verifier):** Every sample Activity that holds a player (VisualizerActivity, MainActivity, ComposeInteropActivity, ComposeVideoActivity, ComposeSwapActivity) sets configChanges in the manifest, so the Activity-scoped player survives rotation only by opting out of recreation. README.md 216-218 and rememberKitePlayer's KDoc both tell apps to hold the player in a ViewModel through rotation, but no sample module demonstrates that pattern, and the Android sample README does not mention rotation at all. (Attaching the renderer from a Dispatchers.Default coroutine is covered by KitePlayer's documented contract that any thread or coroutine may call it, so that part is not a gap.)

**Finder's original claim:** The samples model usage correctly and leak nothing: every player is closed in `shutdown()` from onDestroy, the view is released before the player closes, and the Compose paths let composition own the renderer. But the one hard ownership question on Android, surviving Activity recreation, is answered in the README with a ViewModel and in the samples by turning recreation off, so no sample demonstrates the recommended pattern, and the renderer attach from a Default-dispatcher coroutine works only because `attachRenderer` posts a command, which the samples do not say.

**Scenario:** A reader copies the sample's Activity-scoped `SampleController` without the manifest's `configChanges` and loses playback on every rotation; the README says to use a ViewModel but no sample shows it.

**Impact:** No defect; a gap between what the README recommends and what the samples demonstrate.

**Suggested fix:** Add one sample screen that keeps the KitePlayer in a ViewModel (closed in onCleared) with `KitePlayerVideo`, and drop `configChanges` from that Activity so rotation is exercised.

**How to check it yourself:** Run `grep -n configChanges kiteplayer-sample-android/src/AndroidManifest.xml` (expect five activities, every one that holds a player) and `grep -rn ViewModel kiteplayer-sample*/ --include=*.kt` (expect no hits). Then read README.md 216-218 and RememberKitePlayer.kt 24-26 for the ViewModel advice that nothing demonstrates.

**Verifier's note:** The cited line numbers are stale but every quoted fact exists. The manifest is kiteplayer-sample-android/src/AndroidManifest.xml (not at the module root): line 34 `android:configChanges="orientation|screenSize|screenLayout|keyboardHidden"` on VisualizerActivity, line 52 `android:configChanges="orientation|screenSize|smallestScreenSize|screenLayout"` on MainActivity, lines 57, 62 and 67 `android:configChanges="orientation|screenSize"` on ComposeInteropActivity, ComposeVideoActivity and ComposeSwapActivity. Only SampleLauncherActivity (line 41-45) has none, and it holds no player. SampleController.kt line 44 `private val scope = CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.Default)`, line 49 `val player: KitePlayer = createPlayer(hardwareDecode)` under the comment `One Activity-scoped player`, and lines 80-86 `fun openNormally(renderer: VideoRenderer? = null) { ... scope.launch { renderer?.let(player::attachRenderer); player.open(...) } }`. ComposeVideoActivity.kt lines 57-61 `LaunchedEffect(player, videoState) { withFrameNanos { }; controller.openNormally(videoState.renderer) }`, and lines 119-125 close the player in onDestroy via `controller.shutdown()`. README.md lines 216-218 read exactly as quoted, and RememberKitePlayer.kt lines 24-26 repeat the advice (`Hold the player in a ViewModel when it must outlive that.`). A grep for `ViewModel` across every sample module (kiteplayer-sample-android, kiteplayer-sample, kiteplayer-sample-shared) finds nothing; the only hits in the repository are README.md and RememberKitePlayer.kt. The samples' own README says only `Each screen owns its own player` (kiteplayer-sample-android/README.md line 30) and nothing about rotation. So the gap is real: the recommended pattern is documented twice and demonstrated nowhere, and the samples survive rotation only by opting out of recreation. One part overreaches: the attach from a Default-dispatcher coroutine is not an unstated accident. KitePlayer.kt lines 35-36 state `Calling from any thread or coroutine is safe and no two callers can race each other`, and attachRenderer's KDoc at line 1721 says `The call returns as soon as the request is queued.` That is the public contract, so the samples rely on documented behaviour rather than on an implementation detail. Severity info is right; this is a sample-coverage and docs point, not a defect.

**Severity:** low · **Kind:** Documentation · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** spi/audio · **Lane:** engine-subtitles-output-tail · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

**Where:**

- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/spi/AudioSink.kt:152-163`
- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/spi/AudioSink.kt:281-293`

**Evidence:** AudioSink.events KDoc 158-161: '`FormatChangeRequested` becomes an `AudioDeviceChanged` warning naming the request. `Failed` stops the session ... Nothing here rebuilds a sink or recovers a device yet: publish honestly, and expect a warning or a typed failure rather than a repair.' FormatChangeRequested KDoc 286-287: 'The engine opens a new sink from the same factory and plays on through it (#563). It never reconfigures this one'. handleOutputChange (PlaybackCore.kt 6827-6901) does open a new sink.

**Claim:** The member-level summary a sink author reads first says the opposite of what the event's own KDoc and the engine do. A sink author following the summary would not report FormatChangeRequested at all ('expect a warning rather than a repair'), and the #563 path would never run for their platform.

**Scenario:** Anyone writing an AudioSink for a new platform reads the events KDoc.

**Impact:** Wrong guidance on a public SPI.

**Suggested fix:** Rewrite 154-163 to say what each event does now: FormatChangeRequested opens a new sink from the same factory, DeviceLost and DeviceChanged warn, Underrun warns once, Failed fails the player.

**How to check it yourself:** Read AudioSink.kt 154-163 against 280-292.

**Verifier's note:** AudioSink.kt 152-162 (the events KDoc) reads: `FormatChangeRequested becomes an AudioDeviceChanged warning naming the request. Failed stops the session, and the player fails with the event's error. Nothing here rebuilds a sink or recovers a device yet: publish honestly, and expect a warning or a typed failure rather than a repair.` The FormatChangeRequested KDoc at 281-293 reads: `The engine opens a new sink from the same factory and plays on through it (#563). It never reconfigures this one ... A new sink that negotiates the same format is closed again and nothing changes ... When no new sink opens, this one keeps playing and the engine warns AudioDeviceChanged.` PlaybackCore.kt handleOutputChange (6827-6901) does open a new sink: `val prepared = ... prepareAudioPath(lane.decoder, lane.stream)`, `active.audio = prepared.playback; active.sink = prepared.sink`, and the collector at 13761-13762 routes the event there: `is ...FormatChangeRequested -> outputChangeAsked.value = OutputChange(audio, event.detail)`. AudioSinkEventTest 138-340 tests the replacement. The member-level summary is stale and contradicts both the event KDoc and the engine. Line ranges are 152-163 and 281-293, a line off the cited ones.

### F-175 VideoRenderer rule 5 says a lost surface counts frames as dropped, while the engine deliberately counts them as refused

**Severity:** low · **Kind:** Documentation · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** spi/video · **Lane:** engine-subtitles-output-tail · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

**Where:**

- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/spi/VideoRenderer.kt:24-25`
- `kiteplayer-core/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/VideoPlayback.kt:209-226`

**Evidence:** VideoRenderer.kt 24-25: '5. Losing a surface is an event, not an exception. Playback continues, video frames are counted as dropped, and audio keeps playing'. VideoPlayback.kt 212-217: 'A renderer refusal is [refusedFrames] and is deliberately not counted here. The two are different diagnoses with different fixes'. The present path at 507-513 increments `refused++` when present returns false, not droppedLate.

**Claim:** The SPI's rule list, which is the text a renderer author reads, names the wrong counter. A reader of PlaybackStats.droppedFramesLate during a surface loss sees nothing move and concludes the renderer is still drawing.

**Scenario:** A renderer author or an application debugging a black surface reads rule 5 and watches droppedFramesLate.

**Impact:** Misleading public documentation on a counter meant for diagnosis.

**Suggested fix:** Change rule 5 to 'counted as refused (PlaybackStats.refusedFrames)'.

**How to check it yourself:** Read VideoRenderer.kt 24-25 and VideoPlayback.kt 212-226.

**Verifier's note:** VideoRenderer.kt 24-25: `5. Losing a surface is an event, not an exception. Playback continues, video frames are counted as dropped, and audio keeps playing, because a minimised window should not stop the sound.` VideoPlayback.kt 209-226: `Frames the SCHEDULE dropped because their time had passed. A renderer refusal is [refusedFrames] and is deliberately not counted here. The two are different diagnoses with different fixes ... folding them together made a dead surface look like a slow decoder.` and `Frames a renderer was handed and refused, for example because its surface is gone.` The present path at 505-511 does `if (renderer.present(frame, targetNanos)) { submitted++ ... } else { refused++ }`, never droppedLate. The public stats carry both: PlayerState.kt 362 `val droppedFramesLate: Long = 0` and 372 `val refusedFrames: Long = 0`, with 366 `Counted apart from [droppedFramesLate], which it used to be folded into.` Rule 5 describes the pre-split behaviour and names the wrong counter. Docs only, low severity is right.

### F-091 FlashGuardReachTest passes a drawing that dims by only eight percent at half the allowed light

**Severity:** low · **Kind:** Test gap · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** audioviz/tests · **Lane:** audioviz · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** medium

**Where:**

- `kiteplayer-audioviz/test@jvm/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/audioviz/FlashGuardReachTest.kt:45-62`
- `kiteplayer-audioviz/test@jvm/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/audioviz/FlashGuardReachTest.kt:141-150`
- `kiteplayer-audioviz/test@jvm/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/audioviz/FlashGuardReachTest.kt:155-161`
- `scripts/audioviz-tests.sh:14`

**Evidence:** FlashGuardReachTest.kt 165: `val stubborn = rows.filter { (_, full, half) -> full > MINIMUM && half > full * MOST_SHARE }` with 266 `const val MINIMUM = 0.01f` and 269 `const val MOST_SHARE = 0.92f`. The test renders at DriverProbe.WIDTH x HEIGHT (128 x 80) and 64 x 40 for shaders and compares the mean luma of one frame (line 144-152).

**Claim (as corrected by the verifier):** FlashGuardReachTest's main check only requires the last frame's mean luma at half light to fall below 0.92 of full, which a drawing that scales a small share of its picture (and none of its hit flashes) by lightScale would pass. The brightest-marks check that would catch flashes drawn at full strength runs for only Thin Ice and Ocean Mist, and the only per-drawing measurement of the guard's actual effect, FlashCaptureTest, is in the 25-minute survey and not in the gate.

**Finder's original claim:** The contract in CLAUDE.md and the rendering document is that every drawing multiplies its light by lightScale so the guard can hold a flash. A drawing that applied lightScale to a tenth of its picture would drop its mean luma by about five percent and pass this test. The 0.92 threshold proves only that some light reaches the guard, not that enough does to hold a flash; the quantity that matters for the policy (how much of a swing the guard can take out) is never measured per drawing.

**Scenario:** A new or edited drawing that scales its background by lightScale but draws its hit flashes at full strength passes FlashGuardReachTest, and the only test that would catch it is the 25-minute survey FlashCaptureTest, which is not in the gate.

**Impact:** The gate gives a false sense that the guard's reach is verified; the real verification runs only in the survey.

**Suggested fix:** Measure the ratio the guard needs: render at lightScale 1 and 0.25 and require the half-render's mean luma to fall by close to the same share the drawing's own light contract implies (for example half <= full * 0.6 for drawings whose light is lightFor(energy) * lightScale), or better, feed each drawing a synthetic flash train through the surface with the guard on and count flashes in the output with AreaFlashes at small size, which is fast enough for the gate.

**How to check it yourself:** Run FlashGuardReachTest alone and read the printed `light <name>: full ..., half ..., share ...` lines; a share well above 0.5 marks a drawing whose light only partly follows lightScale. Then extend `theBrightestMarksOfThinIceAndOceanMistFollowTheAllowedLight` to every catalogue entry and see which drawings fail the 0.4 ratio; those are the ones the guard cannot hold strongly. Compare with FlashCaptureTest's per-drawing counts from the last survey report.

**Verifier's note:** The cited lines have drifted but the evidence is there: FlashGuardReachTest.kt 56 `val stubborn = rows.filter { (_, full, half) -> full > MINIMUM && half > full * MOST_SHARE }`, 157 `const val MINIMUM = 0.01f`, 160 `const val MOST_SHARE = 0.92f`, with 'Half the light must leave clearly less than the full picture. *Judgement.*' above it. meanLuma (20-43) renders 150 frames and reads the mean luma of the last frame only, at DriverProbe sizes. A drawing whose light fully followed lightScale would show a share near 0.5 at half light; 0.92 admits one where roughly a sixth of the luma follows the scale, so the arithmetic in the claim holds. Two things the finding leaves out narrow it: the same file also has `theGroundFollowsTheAllowedLightToo` (100: `half > full * 0.75f`) for grounds, and `theBrightestMarksOfThinIceAndOceanMistFollowTheAllowedLight` (142-150, `quarter <= full * 0.4f`), which measures the 99.5th percentile luma, but only for those two named drawings. So 'never measured per drawing' is true for the hit flashes of the other thirteen drawings, and the per-drawing policy outcome is measured only by FlashCaptureTest, which docs/audioviz-rendering-api.md 527-531 places in `./scripts/audioviz-tests.sh survey` and not in the gate (scripts/audioviz-tests.sh line 14 lists it under survey). The docs (510-512, 575-577) state the contract exactly as the finding says: the guard works only through lightScale and this test is the proof that the light reaches every drawing. The finding's framing as a test-gap of low severity is fair; the threshold is a stated judgement and the gap is real.

### F-098 ReopenDeviceTest is allowed a second run in CI and both runs count as the result

**Severity:** low · **Kind:** Test gap · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** ci/android · **Lane:** build-distribution-tests-ci · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

**Where:**

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:825-835`
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:905`
- `kiteplayer-compose-video/android-device-test/kotlin/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/compose/ReopenDeviceTest.kt:85-97`

**Evidence:** ci.yml:826-831: `if [ "$status" != "$before" ]; then echo "::warning::ReopenDeviceTest failed, so it runs once more (#301)"; echo "rerun=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; status=$before; run_tests "$compose_pkg" -e class ...ReopenDeviceTest; fi`. The test itself carries `/** The longest stall measured in a stop on the emulator was 17.6 s (#301). */` (line 146). #301 is not among the open issues of the tracker given to this audit.

**Claim:** A failure of the one device test that measures reopen latency is reset (`status=$before`) and the test is run again; only the second result decides the job. The rerun is surfaced as a warning and in the summary, which is better than most retries, but it still means a real regression in reopen time passes whenever the second run is quick, and the issue it is parked under appears to be closed, so the allowance has no owner.

**Scenario:** A change makes the second open take 12 s instead of 2 s on one run in two. The first run fails, the rerun passes, the job is green with a yellow warning nobody reads in a 45-minute run.

**Impact:** The flakiest device test is also the one least able to fail.

**Suggested fix:** Either keep the retry but fail when the rerun's measured latency is above the bound too (compare numbers, not pass/fail), or move the emulator-stall allowance into the test as an explicit emulator-only timeout as GaplessVideoQueueDeviceTest already does, and remove the rerun. Re-open or re-link the issue that owns the allowance.

**How to check it yourself:** Read ci.yml:823-835 and 905, 926-934. Confirm #301 is closed with `gh api repos/yuroyami/KitePlayer/issues/301 --jq .state`. To see the gap, note that `status=$before` precedes the second `run_tests`, so a first-run failure never reaches `exit $status`.

**Verifier's note:** The cited lines are exact. ci.yml:825-831: `before=$status` ... `if [ "$status" != "$before" ]; then echo "::warning::ReopenDeviceTest failed, so it runs once more (#301)"; echo "rerun=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; status=$before; run_tests ... ReopenDeviceTest; fi`. `run_tests` sets `status=1` only when the part log lacks `^OK (`, so after `status=$before` only the second run decides `exit $status` (line 835). ReopenDeviceTest.kt:146 carries `/** The longest stall measured in a stop on the emulator was 17.6 s (#301). */`. `gh api repos/yuroyami/KitePlayer/issues/301` answers `state: closed`, `closed_at: 2026-10-02`, title `On the Android emulator, a stop on the Compose GPU path can wait 16 s inside MediaCodec.stop`, so the allowance is parked under a closed issue. The retry is deliberate and visible: ci.yml:657 `The one allowance left is the second run of ReopenDeviceTest inside its step (#301)`, line 905 prints a summary line when `REOPEN_RERUN` is true, and lines 926 and 934 collect logs and upload reports on a rerun. None of that changes the job's exit status, so the claim holds. One nuance: on the emulator the test already holds only the open (not the stop) to `firstMs + 3_000` (ReopenDeviceTest.kt:85-97), so the rerun covers the open-latency assertion too, which is the regression the finding describes.

### F-099 The visualiser's picture-level regression suites never run in CI

**Severity:** low · **Kind:** Test gap · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** ci/audioviz · **Lane:** build-distribution-tests-ci · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high · **Related open issue:** #682

**Where:**

- `scripts/audioviz-tests.sh:13-24`
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:343-346`

**Evidence:** audioviz-tests.sh:13-17 lists `RENDERING_SUITES=( DensityTest ScreenMotionTest ChangeTest DriverInjectionTest FlashCaptureTest DriverMatrixReport MappingQualificationTest MoodRenderTest DrawCostTest RecipeTest ContactSheetTest PostSheetTest RenderPerformanceTest DesktopRenderPerformanceTest )` and line 24 excludes every one of them in `gate`. ci.yml:346 runs `./scripts/audioviz-tests.sh gate` and nothing runs `survey`; a grep of ci.yml for `survey` finds no hit.

**Claim:** The suites that measure what a viewer sees (density, motion on screen, scene changes, flash capture, mood rendering, draw cost) are only run by a person who types `survey` and waits 25 minutes. The CI gate runs the unit-level and the two invariant suites (PausedPictureTest, FlashGuardReachTest are not excluded), so a drawing that regresses in density or motion ships with every job green. The owner's own document says a pass that cannot catch a pass-that-does-nothing is the failure mode of render passes.

**Scenario:** A shader change makes one drawing render nearly static (a known failure shape per CLAUDE.md: a pass that compiles, costs every tap and does nothing). ScreenMotionTest would fail; the gate does not run it; the release ships it. Open issues #681 to #683 ask for more measurement, but even the measurements that exist are not scheduled.

**Impact:** Regressions in the visualiser's visible behaviour reach releases unobserved, and the 25-minute suite only grows staler.

**Suggested fix:** Add a scheduled or nightly job (or a second macOS job in publish.yml) that runs `audioviz-tests.sh survey` and uploads the report, or split the survey so the cheapest picture checks (ChangeTest, ScreenMotionTest, DensityTest at reduced size) join the gate.

**How to check it yourself:** grep -n survey .github/workflows/*.yml returns nothing. Run `./scripts/audioviz-tests.sh gate` locally and confirm DensityTest and ScreenMotionTest do not appear in build/reports.

**Verifier's note:** scripts/audioviz-tests.sh:13-17 lists RENDERING_SUITES exactly as quoted (DensityTest, ScreenMotionTest, ChangeTest, DriverInjectionTest, FlashCaptureTest, DriverMatrixReport, MappingQualificationTest, MoodRenderTest, DrawCostTest, RecipeTest, ContactSheetTest, PostSheetTest, RenderPerformanceTest, DesktopRenderPerformanceTest) and lines 21-24 exclude each in `gate`: `for suite in "${RENDERING_SUITES[@]}"; do filters+=("--exclude-classes=*.$suite"); done`. ci.yml:346 runs `./scripts/audioviz-tests.sh gate`; the only other hit for 'survey' in .github is the comment at ci.yml:333-334, `audioviz runs through its gate script, which leaves out the long rendering surveys`, which shows the omission is deliberate for time, not an oversight. .github/workflows holds only central-consumer.yml, ci.yml, docs.yml and publish.yml, none scheduled, none running survey. PausedPictureTest and FlashGuardReachTest exist under kiteplayer-audioviz/test@jvm and are not in the excluded list, so the gate does run those two invariant suites. The test-gap claim holds as stated; the trade-off (25 minutes) is acknowledged in the CI comment, which the owner may want to mention when posting. Related to #682 but not a duplicate: #682 asks for a cost budget, this is about scheduling the existing suites.

### F-100 In CI the native halves of the JVM jar can drop out silently, and the size ratchet reports it as a note

**Severity:** low · **Kind:** Test gap · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** ci/publish · **Lane:** build-distribution-tests-ci · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

**Where:**

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:226-233`
- `build-plugins/libass-native/src/libassNative.kt:82-106`
- `build-plugins/build-support/src/LibassAdapters.kt:112-118`
- `scripts/check-artifact-size.sh:25-31`
- `artifact-size-baseline.txt:43`

**Evidence:** libassNative.kt:135: `val requireAll = System.getenv("KITEPLAYER_LIBASS_REQUIRE_ALL_HOST_JNI") == "true"`; lines 150-153: `if (!LibassAdapters.hostToolchainReady(host, dataDir)) { if (requireAll) throw ...; log("jvm jar skips the $host adapter: no konan sysroot for $konanTarget yet..."); continue }`. ci.yml:232-233 runs `./scripts/check-artifact-size.sh` with no env, and the variable appears nowhere in ci.yml. check-artifact-size.sh:30: `A line more than ten percent below its baseline passes with a note.` Baseline `kiteplayer-libass jvm 5267358` is four JNI libraries; one missing would read as a shrink.

**Claim:** On the CI macOS runner the Linux and Windows JNI adapters of the libass JVM jar are linked only if the konan sysroots happen to be present; otherwise the plugin logs and skips, and the one check that looks at the artifact's size turns a 25 percent shrink into a note. The verify-central-consumer job checks only the macOS arm64 half. So a sysroot provisioning change can make every CI run green while the jar CI measured is missing a platform; the release is guarded (publish.yml sets the flag) but the signal that CI is supposed to give before a release is not.

**Scenario:** A Kotlin bump renames the mingw sysroot package; `hostToolchainReady` returns false on the runner; the jar measured in CI has three adapters; CI passes with `note: lower the baseline`; the maintainer lowers the baseline believing the strip in #615 shrank it.

**Impact:** The ratchet that exists to notice native payload changes cannot notice a lost payload, and the first hard failure moves to the release run.

**Suggested fix:** Set KITEPLAYER_LIBASS_REQUIRE_ALL_HOST_JNI=true (and the Android flag) in the macos-host job so CI builds what the release builds, and make a shrink of more than the limit fail for the lines that carry native code, or add an explicit content check (unzip and expect each manifest.txt) after the size step.

**How to check it yourself:** `grep -n REQUIRE_ALL_HOST_JNI .github/workflows/ci.yml .github/workflows/publish.yml` (publish only). Read libassNative.kt:82-106 and LibassAdapters.kt:112-118. Locally, move `~/.konan/dependencies/<msys2-mingw-w64-x86_64-*>` aside, build kiteplayer-libass for jvm, `unzip -l` the jar for `kiteplayer-libass-native/windows-x64/`, then run `./scripts/check-artifact-size.sh` and read the note.

**Verifier's note:** The libassNative.kt lines drifted: libassNative.kt:82 `val requireAll = System.getenv("KITEPLAYER_LIBASS_REQUIRE_ALL_HOST_JNI") == "true"`; 96-100 `if (requireAll && konanTarget != null) CompileKiteRt.ensureToolchain(...)` then `if (!LibassAdapters.hostToolchainReady(host, dataDir)) { if (requireAll) throw BuildFailure(...); log("jvm jar skips the $host adapter: no konan sysroot for $konanTarget yet..."); continue }`, and 101-106 skip the same way when no chain is found. LibassAdapters.kt:112-118 `hostToolchainReady` for linux and windows is only `konanDataDir.resolve("dependencies").resolve(sysroot).isDirectory`. `grep -n REQUIRE_ALL .github/workflows/ci.yml` returns nothing; the variable is set only in publish.yml:155 and 182. ci.yml:232-233 runs `./scripts/check-artifact-size.sh` with no env, and check-artifact-size.sh:30 says `A line more than ten percent below its baseline passes with a note`; artifact-size-baseline.txt:43 is `kiteplayer-libass jvm 5267358`. The ratchets step (ci.yml:138-150) compiles every platform, so on a warm `~/.konan` cache the sysroots are usually present, but nothing orders the linux and mingw compiles before the libass jar task on a cold cache, and nothing afterwards counts the adapters in the jar. Two corrections: there is no job named verify-central-consumer; the step is `Published-format Native consumer and HTTPS` at ci.yml:226-229, which runs `verify-network-distribution.sh --run --target macos` only. The Linux job (linux-jvm-android, ci.yml:499) builds its own jar on Linux and the only JNI presence check in CI (ci.yml:596-600) is for the Android APK, not the JVM jar.

**Severity:** low · **Kind:** Test gap · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** ci/windows · **Lane:** build-distribution-tests-ci · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

**Where:**

- `scripts/check-test-coverage.py:24-33`

The gate's `windows()` link list (check-gate.sh:156-158) also omits io.

**Claim (as corrected by the verifier):** kiteplayer-io publishes a mingwX64 klib whose only common code is ReadSlice and MediaIoException, and its two concrete common tests (ReadSliceTest) compile for mingwX64 but are run by no CI job and linked by no gate step; the 11 contract tests in the same folder are abstract and have no Windows subclass. scripts/check-test-coverage.py reads only eight platform folders, none for mingwX64, linuxX64 or linuxArm64, so this gap and any future one on those platforms is invisible to it.

**Finder's original claim:** kiteplayer-io ships a mingwX64 klib and the 13 common tests of the module compile for it but are run by no job and no gate step. The checker that was written to stop this class of gap (#637) only reads eight folder names, none of them a Windows or Linux platform, so a future module that gains a Windows platform and tests is equally invisible.

**Scenario:** A change to kiteplayer-io's common code that relies on a POSIX-only behaviour (path separators, a `/` prefix check) breaks the Windows klib; every job stays green; a native Windows consumer finds it.

**Impact:** A published platform of a published module with zero executed tests, in a repository whose stated rule is that compilation is not support.

**Suggested fix:** Add `-m kiteplayer-io` to the Windows job and to check-gate.sh windows(). Extend check-test-coverage.py to derive platforms from each module.yaml and to require that every platform CI executes (mingwX64, linuxX64, linuxArm64, the tvOS and watchOS simulators) is named for every module that has tests compiling for it.

**How to check it yourself:** grep -n 'kiteplayer-io' .github/workflows/ci.yml and see no hit in the mingwX64 job (lines 1145-1149). Count the tests that would run: `grep -c @Test kiteplayer-io/test/*/**/ReadSliceTest.kt` gives 2, and the abstract contract classes have subclasses only outside the common folder. Adding `-m kiteplayer-io` to the Windows job and a `test` (common) entry or mingwX64 entry to FOLDERS in check-test-coverage.py closes both halves.

**Verifier's note:** The gap is real but smaller than written. ci.yml:1145-1149 runs `kotlin.bat test -p mingwX64 -m kiteplayer-core -m kiteplayer-subtitles -m kiteplayer-output -m kiteplayer-rt -m kiteplayer-libass -m kiteplayer`, no kiteplayer-io, and scripts/check-gate.sh:154-159 windows() links the same six without io. kiteplayer-io/module.yaml lists mingwX64 among its platforms. scripts/check-test-coverage.py:24-33 FOLDERS has only test@jvm, test@android, test@ios, test@iosSimulatorArm64, test@macos, test@macosArm64, test@wasmJs and test@js, and main() at lines 90-95 reads only those folders, so a Windows or Linux-only gap cannot be reported. Two corrections. First, the count: kiteplayer-io/test/ holds ReadSliceTest (2 @Test, a concrete class) and MediaIoContractTest.kt (11 @Test inside `abstract class ForwardMediaIoContractTest` at line 19 and `abstract class MediaIoContractTest` at line 114). Every concrete subclass lives in test@posix, test@jvmAndAndroid, test@jvm, test@apple or the device tests; the posix alias in module.yaml excludes mingwX64, so on Windows only ReadSliceTest's 2 tests would run. Second, the scenario: kiteplayer-io's common src holds only ReadSlice.kt and MediaIoException.kt, and there is no src@mingw, so the mingwX64 klib has no file door at all and a POSIX path-handling bug cannot reach it. linuxX64 does run kiteplayer-io (ci.yml:966), so the checker's blindness to Linux is a design limit with no present gap behind it.

**Where:**

- `kiteplayer-compose-ui/src@ios/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/compose/HoldDisplayAwake.ios.kt:22-43`
- `kiteplayer-view/src@ios/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/view/IdleTimerHolds.kt:15-37`

- `kiteplayer-compose-ui/src/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/compose/KitePlayerControls.kt:214-218`
- `kiteplayer-compose-ui/test@jvm/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/compose/ControlsUiTest.kt:297-306`

**Evidence:** Two `private object IdleTimerHolds` with the same `KEY = "io.github.yuroyami.kiteplayer.idleTimerHolds"`: compose-ui's calls `UIApplication.sharedApplication.idleTimerDisabled` directly (403, 410) and has no test seam; the view's has `internal var setIdleTimerDisabled` (420) and an `IdleTimerHoldsTest`. compose-ui has no test directory for iOS or Android at all (only `test@jvm`), so `HoldDisplayAwake.android`'s `ScreenOnHolds` and `KeepDisplayAwakeWhilePlaying` are unverified. ControlsUiTest 297-306 tests Escape only on the Speed menu, whose button never disappears.

**Claim:** The display-awake counting is the kind of shared mutable singleton that breaks when one copy changes (for example if one side adds a floor at zero or a different key), and only one of the two copies is under test. The one crash path found in the Compose controls (menu focus return) is in the untested half of the menu behaviour.

**Scenario:** A later edit to the view's IdleTimerHolds key or semantics silently splits the count: a Compose canvas video releases the timer while a native view still plays, and no test notices.

**Impact:** Regression risk without signal.

**Suggested fix:** Move the iOS counter into one internal object in kiteplayer-view (compose-ui already depends on it) and delete the copy; add an Android host test for ScreenOnHolds (two holds, one release, keepScreenOn stays true); add the Escape-after-button-vanished case to ControlsUiTest.

**How to check it yourself:** `grep -rn "idleTimerHolds" kiteplayer-compose-ui kiteplayer-view` shows two objects; `ls kiteplayer-compose-ui/test*` shows only test@jvm.

**Verifier's note:** Line numbers are wrong (both files are under 45 lines) but the evidence is real. HoldDisplayAwake.ios.kt lines 22-43: `private object IdleTimerHolds` with `KEY = "io.github.yuroyami.kiteplayer.idleTimerHolds"` and direct `UIApplication.sharedApplication.idleTimerDisabled = true/false` at lines 28 and 35, with no seam. IdleTimerHolds.kt lines 15-37: `internal object IdleTimerHolds`, same KEY, `internal var setIdleTimerDisabled` at line 19, tested by kiteplayer-view/test@ios/.../IdleTimerHoldsTest.kt. `ls` shows kiteplayer-compose-ui has only `test@jvm` while kiteplayer-view has test@android, test@apple, test@ios, test@jvm, test@macos, test@wasmJs; so `ScreenOnHolds` (HoldDisplayAwake.android.kt lines 21-39) and `KeepDisplayAwakeWhilePlaying` (KitePlayerVideo.kt lines 169-173) have no test anywhere. Both copies comment that they are twins sharing one key (HoldDisplayAwake.ios.kt lines 18-21, IdleTimerHolds.kt lines 11-13), which is exactly the coupling the finding says is one-sided under test. ControlsUiTest lines 297-306 is the only Escape test and uses the Speed button, whose `shown` is `speed.options.isNotEmpty()` (KitePlayerControls.kt line 313); the Audio, Subtitles and Quality buttons can be absent (lines 300-309, `MenuButton` returns at line 465 `if (!shown) return` before attaching its FocusRequester), and `LaunchedEffect(returnFocusTo)` at lines 214-218 calls `menuButtons.getValue(menu).requestFocus()` unconditionally. Whether that requestFocus on an unattached requester throws is asserted by the finding from elsewhere and was not verified here; the test-gap statement stands on its own.

### F-028 No test reads the position through a pause or Ended on media whose audio ends before its picture

**Severity:** medium · **Kind:** Test gap · **Repo:** KitePlayer · **Area:** core/clock · **Lane:** engine-seek-sync-tracks · **Verdict:** CONFIRMED · **Finder confidence:** high

**Where:**

- `kiteplayer-core/test/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/EarlyStreamEndTest.kt:38-55`
- `kiteplayer-core/test/io/github/yuroyami/kiteplayer/AudioPausePositionTest.kt:50-70`

**Evidence:** EarlyStreamEndTest.aSoundThatEndsBeforeThePictureLeavesThePicturePlaying asserts the position only while playing (`val midway = harness.core.position()...; assertTrue(abs(midway - 20_000_000) < 500_000` at 46-47) and then only the status at the end (`assertEquals(PlaybackStatus.Ended, harness.core.snapshots.value.status)` at 49). AudioPausePositionTest pauses only while real audio is still being rendered (the loop at 58-62 renders 14 blocks of submitted audio before `audio.pause()`).

**Claim (as corrected by the verifier):** The scripted fixture for an audio stream that ends before the picture (EarlyStreamEndTest.shortSound) exists, but no test reads position() after a pause in the silent tail, after Ended, or after a setSpeed made once the sound has ended. The #646 pause rule in AudioPlayback.anchorLocked is tested only against a device still publishing anchors (AudioPausePositionTest), and nothing covers the case where the clock has run on past the ring's last anchor, which is where that rule can pull a paused or ended position back to the last sound.

**Finder's original claim:** The scripted fixture that exercises an early audio end exists and would expose the position snap-back and the speed-change loss with two assertions, but neither test reads position() after a pause in the silent tail, after Ended, or after a setSpeed made after the sound ended. The clock rule from #646 was tested only against a device that was still publishing anchors.

**Scenario:** Add to EarlyStreamEndTest: pause at 20 s and assert position() stays near 20 s; run to Ended and assert position() is near 40 s; setSpeed(2.0) at 10 s and assert position() near 30 s ten seconds later.

**Impact:** The two clock defects in this report ship untested, and any fix to anchorLocked can regress silently.

**Suggested fix:** Add the three assertions above to EarlyStreamEndTest, and an AudioPausePositionTest case that marks the ring ending, renders silence for a second (no anchor), pauses, and asserts the position did not move back.

**How to check it yourself:** Add to EarlyStreamEndTest on shortSound(): (a) run 20 s, pause(), run 1 s, assert position() within 500 ms of 20 s; (b) run to Ended, assert position() within 500 ms of 40 s; (c) at 10 s setSpeed(2.0), run 10 s, assert position() near 30 s. Run `./kotlin test -m kiteplayer-core -p jvm` and check the report lists EarlyStreamEndTest with the new test count, since a module with no matching tests still exits zero.

**Verifier's note:** The cited evidence is exact. EarlyStreamEndTest.aSoundThatEndsBeforeThePictureLeavesThePicturePlaying (38-55) reads position only while playing: `val midway = harness.core.position().inWholeMicroseconds` / `assertTrue(abs(midway - 20_000_000) < 500_000, ...)` (46-47), then after `harness.run(25.seconds)` asserts only `assertEquals(PlaybackStatus.Ended, harness.core.snapshots.value.status)` (49). No test in that class calls pause() or setSpeed(); the only other position read is after a seek while playing (aSeekBackFromAfterTheSoundEndedPlaysTheSoundAgain, 199-201). AudioPausePositionTest (50-70) is a unit test of AudioPlayback alone, pausing after 14 rendered blocks of real submitted audio (`repeat(14) { sink.render!!.onRender(...) }` at 58-62, then `audio.pause()`), i.e. with the device still publishing anchors. I searched the whole kiteplayer-core test tree: the only other users of packetEndUs are LateStreamTest and MissionAAudioFastPathRiskTest, neither of which pauses, changes speed or reads position after an audio stream has ended early; no test reads position() after PlaybackStatus.Ended except RedrawTest (76), on ordinary media. The gap is real. The mechanism the gap would cover is also visible in AudioPlayback.anchorLocked (729-746): when `playoutClock.paused`, the ring's last anchor is applied whenever `heardNow < frozen`; the anchor floor (`anchorFloorNanos`, set only in play() at 795 and cleared at 733 by the first newer anchor) does not protect a first play, so after the sound ends at 3 s and the clock runs on to 20 s, a pause can read the clock back to the 3 s anchor. And handleEof itself calls `session.audio?.anchorClock(); session.audio?.pause()` (PlaybackCore 9265-9266) on the same path. I did not trace whether currentPosition() (13618-13634) falls back to the video reading first in that state, since `session.audio?.takeIf { session.audioLane != null }` still wins under the default master clock, so I state the defect as likely rather than proven; the test gap itself is confirmed. Medium severity for a test gap on #646 behaviour is defensible given the owner's rule that device bugs are reproduced in the JVM harness first.
